2.67.m: Alarka, best of the Kāśis, remained young and endowed with beauty; / by the grace of Lopāmudrā he obtained supreme longevity.'

2.67.s:
śāpasyānte mahābāhurhatvā kṣemakarākṣasam /
ramyāmāvāsayāmāsa purīṃ vārāṇasīṃ nṛpaḥ //
2.67.d:
शापस्यान्ते महाबाहुर्हत्वा क्षेमकराक्षसम् ।
रम्यामावासयामास पुरीं वाराणसीं नृपः ॥
2.67.m: At the end of the curse, the mighty-armed king, having slain the rākṣasa Kṣemaka, / settled the delightful city of Vārāṇasī.

2.67.s:
sannaterapi dāyādaḥ sunītho nāma dhārmikaḥ /
sunīthasya tu dāyādaḥ kṣaimākhyo nāma dhārmikaḥ //
2.67.d:
सन्नतेरपि दायादः सुनीथो नाम धार्मिकः ।
सुनीथस्य तु दायादः क्षैमाख्यो नाम धार्मिकः ॥
2.67.m: The heir of Sannati was the righteous Sunītha. / The heir of Sunītha was the righteous one named Kṣema.

2.67.s:
kṣemasya ketumānputraḥ suketustasya cātmajaḥ /
suketutanayaścāpi dharmaketuriti śrutaḥ //
2.67.d:
क्षेमस्य केतुमान्पुत्रः सुकेतुस्तस्य चात्मजः ।
सुकेतुतनयश्चापि धर्मकेतुरिति श्रुतः ॥
2.67.m: The son of Kṣema was Ketumān, and his son was Suketu. / And the son of Suketu is renowned as Dharmaketu.

2.67.s:
dharmaketostu dāyādaḥ satyaketurmahārathaḥ /
satyaketusutaścāpi vibhurnāma prajeśvaraḥ //
2.67.d:
धर्मकेतोस्तु दायादः सत्यकेतुर्महारथः ।
सत्यकेतुसुतश्चापि विभुर्नाम प्रजेश्वरः ॥
2.67.m: The heir of Dharmaketu was the great chariot-warrior Satyaketu. / And the son of Satyaketu was the lord of subjects named Vibhu.

2.67.s:
suvibhustu vibhoḥ putraḥ sukumārastataḥ smṛtaḥ /
sukumārasya putrastu dhṛṣṭaketuḥ sudhārmikaḥ //
2.67.d:
सुविभुस्तु विभोः पुत्रः सुकुमारस्ततः स्मृतः ।
सुकुमारस्य पुत्रस्तु धृष्टकेतुः सुधार्मिकः ॥
2.67.m: Suvibhu was the son of Vibhu; from him is remembered Sukumāra. / And the son of Sukumāra was the very righteous Dhṛṣṭaketu.

2.67.s:
dhṛṣṭaketostu dāyādo veṇuhotraḥ prajeśvaraḥ /
veṇuhotrasutaścāpi gārgyo vai nāma viśrutaḥ //
2.67.d:
धृष्टकेतोस्तु दायादो वेणुहोत्रः प्रजेश्वरः ।
वेणुहोत्रसुतश्चापि गार्ग्यो वै नाम विश्रुतः ॥
2.67.m: The heir of Dhṛṣṭaketu was the lord of subjects Veṇuhotra. / And the son of Veṇuhotra was the renowned Gārgya.

2.67.s:
gārgyasya gargabhūmistu vaṃśo vatsasya dhīmataḥ /
brāhmaṇāḥ kṣatriyāścaiva tayoḥ putrāḥ sudhārmikāḥ //
2.67.d:
गार्ग्यस्य गर्गभूमिस्तु वंशो वत्सस्य धीमतः ।
ब्राह्मणाः क्षत्रियाश्चैव तयोः पुत्राः सुधार्मिकाः ॥
2.67.m: Gargabhūmi was [the son] of Gārgya, and [such was] the lineage of the wise Vatsa. / Their sons were very righteous brāhmaṇas and kṣatriyas,

2.67.s:
vikrāntā balavantaśca sihatulyaparākramāḥ /
ityete kāśyapāḥ proktā rajerapi nibodhata //
2.67.d:
विक्रान्ता बलवन्तश्च सिहतुल्यपराक्रमाः ।
इत्येते काश्यपाः प्रोक्ता रजेरपि निबोधत ॥
2.67.m: valorous, strong, and possessing prowess equal to lions. / Thus these Kāśyapas have been declared. Learn also of Raji.

2.67.s:
rajeḥ putraśatānyāsanpañca vīryavato bhuvi /
rājeyamiti vikhyātaṃ kṣatra siṃdrabhayāvaham //
2.67.d:
रजेः पुत्रशतान्यासन्पञ्च वीर्यवतो भुवि ।
राजेयमिति विख्यातं क्षत्र सिंद्रभयावहम् ॥
2.67.m: Powerful Raji had five hundred sons on earth; / they were renowned as the Rājeyas, a kṣatriya [order] bringing terror to Indra.

2.67.s:
tadā devāsure yuddhe samutpanne sudāruṇe /
devāścaivāsurāścaiva pitāmahamathābruvan //
2.67.d:
तदा देवासुरे युद्धे समुत्पन्ने सुदारुणे ।
देवाश्चैवासुराश्चैव पितामहमथाब्रुवन् ॥
2.67.m: Then, when a very terrible battle between gods and asuras arose, / both the gods and the asuras spoke to the Grandfather:

2.67.s:
āvayorbhagavanyuddhe vijetā ko bhaviṣyati /
brūhi naḥ sarvalokeśa śrotumicchāmahe vayam //
2.67.d:
आवयोर्भगवन्युद्धे विजेता को भविष्यति ।
ब्रूहि नः सर्वलोकेश श्रोतुमिच्छामहे वयम् ॥
2.67.m: “O Lord, which of us two shall be victorious in battle? / Tell us, O Lord of all worlds; we wish to hear.”

2.67.s:
brahmovāca /
yeṣāmarthāya saṃgrāme rajirāttāyudhaḥ prabhuḥ /
yotsyate te vijaṣyante trīṃllokānnātra saṃśayaḥ //
2.67.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच ।
येषामर्थाय संग्रामे रजिरात्तायुधः प्रभुः ।
योत्स्यते ते विजष्यन्ते त्रींल्लोकान्नात्र संशयः ॥
2.67.m: Brahmā said: / “Those on whose behalf in battle the powerful Raji fights, having taken up arms, / they shall conquer the three worlds; of this there is no doubt.

2.67.s:
rajiryatastato lakṣmīryato lakṣmīstato dhṛtiḥ /
yato dhṛtistato dharmo yato dharmastato jayaḥ //
2.67.d:
रजिर्यतस्ततो लक्ष्मीर्यतो लक्ष्मीस्ततो धृतिः ।
यतो धृतिस्ततो धर्मो यतो धर्मस्ततो जयः ॥
2.67.m: Where Raji is, there is fortune; where fortune is, there is steadfastness; / where steadfastness is, there is dharma; where dharma is, there is victory.”

2.67.s:
te devā dānavāḥ sarve tataḥ śrutvā rajerjayam /
abhyayurjayamicchantaḥ stuvanto rājasattamam //
2.67.d:
ते देवा दानवाः सर्वे ततः श्रुत्वा रजेर्जयम् ।
अभ्ययुर्जयमिच्छन्तः स्तुवन्तो राजसत्तमम् ॥
2.67.m: Then, having heard of Raji’s victory, all those gods and dānavas, / desiring victory, went [to him], praising the best of kings.

2.67.s:
te hṛṣṭamanasaḥ sarve rājānaṃ devadānavāḥ /
ūcurasmajjayāya tvaṃ gṛhāma varakārmukam //
2.67.d:
ते हृष्टमनसः सर्वे राजानं देवदानवाः ।
ऊचुरस्मज्जयाय त्वं गृहाम वरकार्मुकम् ॥
2.67.m: All those gods and dānavas, delighted in mind, / said to the king: “For our victory, take up your excellent bow!”

2.67.s:
rajiruvāca
ahaṃ jeṣyāmi bho daityā devāñccha krapurogamān /
indro bhavāmi dharmātmā tato yotsye raṇājire //
2.67.d:
रजिरुवाच
अहं जेष्यामि भो दैत्या देवाञ्च्छ क्रपुरोगमान् ।
इन्द्रो भवामि धर्मात्मा ततो योत्स्ये रणाजिरे ॥
2.67.m: Raji said: / “O Daityas! I shall conquer the gods with Indra at their head; / [or] I shall become the righteous Indra, and then I shall fight on the battlefield.”

2.67.s:
dānavā ūcuḥ
asmākamindraḥ prahlādastasyārthe vijayāmahe /
asmintu samaye rājaṃstiṣṭhethā devanodite //
2.67.d:
दानवा ऊचुः
अस्माकमिन्द्रः प्रह्लादस्तस्यार्थे विजयामहे ।
अस्मिन्तु समये राजंस्तिष्ठेथा देवनोदिते ॥
2.67.m: The dānavas said: / “Prahlāda is our Indra; for his sake we conquer. / O King, abide by this agreement prompted by the gods!”

2.67.s:
sa tatheti bruvanneva devairapyabhinoditaḥ /
bhaviṣyasīṃdro jitveti devairapi nimantritaḥ //
2.67.d:
स तथेति ब्रुवन्नेव देवैरप्यभिनोदितः ।
भविष्यसींद्रो जित्वेति देवैरपि निमन्त्रितः ॥
2.67.m: Saying “So be it,” he was also approached by the gods. / He was invited by the gods, [who said,] “Having conquered, you shall become Indra.”

2.67.s:
jaghāna dānavānsarvānye 'vadhyā vajrapāṇayaḥ /
sa vipranaṣṭāṃ devānāṃ paramaśrīḥ śriyaṃ vaśī //
2.67.d:
जघान दानवान्सर्वान्ये ऽवध्या वज्रपाणयः ।
स विप्रनष्टां देवानां परमश्रीः श्रियं वशी ॥
2.67.m: He slew all the dānavas who were invincible to the thunderbolt-bearer. / That self-controlled one of supreme splendour, [recovering] the lost fortune of the gods,

2.67.s:
nihatya dānavānsarvā nājahāra rajiḥ prabhuḥ /
taṃ tathāha rajiṃ tatra devaiḥ saha śatakratuḥ //
2.67.d:
निहत्य दानवान्सर्वा नाजहार रजिः प्रभुः ।
तं तथाह रजिं तत्र देवैः सह शतक्रतुः ॥
2.67.m: having slain all the dānavas, the powerful Raji restored [it]. / There Śatakratu along with the gods spoke thus to Raji:

2.67.s:
rajiputro 'hamityuktvā punarevābrahavīdvacaḥ /
indro 'si rājandevānāṃ sarveṣāṃ nātra saṃśayaḥ //
2.67.d:
रजिपुत्रो ऽहमित्युक्त्वा पुनरेवाब्रहवीद्वचः ।
इन्द्रो ऽसि राजन्देवानां सर्वेषां नात्र संशयः ॥
2.67.m: Having said, “I am Raji’s son,” he spoke these words again: / “You are the Indra of all the gods, O King; of this there is no doubt.

2.67.s:
yasyāhamindraḥ putraste khyātiṃ yāsyāmi śatruhan /
sa tu śakravacaḥ śrutvā vañcitastena māyayā //
2.67.d:
यस्याहमिन्द्रः पुत्रस्ते ख्यातिं यास्यामि शत्रुहन् ।
स तु शक्रवचः श्रुत्वा वञ्चितस्तेन मायया ॥
2.67.m: I, Indra, am your son; I shall attain fame [through you], O slayer of foes!” / But having heard Śakra’s words, he was deceived by him through illusion.

2.67.s:
tathetyevāha vai rājā prīyamāṇaḥ śatakratum /
tasmiṃstu devasadṛśe divaṃ prāpte mahīpatau //
2.67.d:
तथेत्येवाह वै राजा प्रीयमाणः शतक्रतुम् ।
तस्मिंस्तु देवसदृशे दिवं प्राप्ते महीपतौ ॥
2.67.m: Delighted, the king said “So be it” to Śatakratu. / But when that king, equal to a god, went to heaven,

2.67.s:
dāyādyamindrādā jahnurācāryatanayā rajeḥ /
tāni putraśatānyasya tacca sthānaṃ śacīpateḥ //
2.67.d:
दायाद्यमिन्द्रादा जह्नुराचार्यतनया रजेः ।
तानि पुत्रशतान्यस्य तच्च स्थानं शचीपतेः ॥
2.67.m: the sons of Raji, pupils of their teacher, seized the inheritance from Indra— / those hundreds of sons of his, and that realm of Śacī’s husband.

2.67.s:
samākrāmanta bahudhā svargalokaṃ triviṣṭapam /
tataḥ kāle bahutithe samatīte mahābalaḥ //
2.67.d:
समाक्रामन्त बहुधा स्वर्गलोकं त्रिविष्टपम् ।
ततः काले बहुतिथे समतीते महाबलः ॥
2.67.m: They overran heaven, the celestial abode, in many ways. / Then, after much time had passed, the mighty

2.67.s:
hatarājyo 'bravīcchakro hatabhāgo bṛhaspatim /
badarī phalamātraṃ vai puroḍāśaṃ vidhatsva me //
2.67.d:
हतराज्यो ऽब्रवीच्छक्रो हतभागो बृहस्पतिम् ।
बदरी फलमात्रं वै पुरोडाशं विधत्स्व मे ॥
2.67.m: Śakra, deprived of his kingdom and deprived of his sacrificial share, spoke to Bṛhaspati: / “Prepare for me a sacrificial cake measuring only a jujube fruit,

2.67.s:
brahmarṣe yena tiṣṭheyaṃ tejasāpyāyitastataḥ /
brahmankṛśo 'haṃ vimanā tdṛtarājyo hṛtāsanaḥ //
2.67.d:
ब्रह्मर्षे येन तिष्ठेयं तेजसाप्यायितस्ततः ।
ब्रह्मन्कृशो ऽहं विमना त्दृतराज्यो हृतासनः ॥
2.67.m: O brāhmaṇa sage, so that, refreshed by its radiance, I may stand firm! / O brāhmaṇa, I am emaciated, dejected, my kingdom taken, my throne stolen,

2.67.s:
hataujā durbalo yuddhe rajiputreḥ prasīda me /
bṛhaspatiruvāca
yadyevaṃ coditaḥśakra tvayāsyāṃ pūrvameva hi //
2.67.d:
हतौजा दुर्बलो युद्धे रजिपुत्रेः प्रसीद मे ।
बृहस्पतिरुवाच
यद्येवं चोदितःशक्र त्वयास्यां पूर्वमेव हि ॥
2.67.m: my splendour destroyed, weak in battle against Raji's sons. Be gracious to me!” / Bṛhaspati said: / “O Śakra, if indeed I had been urged by you thus earlier,

2.67.s:
nābhaviṣyattvatpriyārthamakarttavyaṃ mamānagha /
prayatiṣyāmi devendra tvaddhitārthaṃ mahādyute //
2.67.d:
नाभविष्यत्त्वत्प्रियार्थमकर्त्तव्यं ममानघ ।
प्रयतिष्यामि देवेन्द्र त्वद्धितार्थं महाद्युते ॥
2.67.m: there would have been nothing undone for your pleasure, O sinless one. / I shall strive for your benefit, O lord of gods, O one of great splendour!

2.67.s:
yajñabhāgaṃ ca rājyaṃ ca acirātpratipatsyase /
tathā śakra gamiṣyāmi mā bhūtte viklavaṃ manaḥ //
2.67.d:
यज्ञभागं च राज्यं च अचिरात्प्रतिपत्स्यसे ।
तथा शक्र गमिष्यामि मा भूत्ते विक्लवं मनः ॥
2.67.m: You shall recover your share of the sacrifice and your kingdom before long. / I shall proceed accordingly, O Śakra; let your mind not be distressed.”

2.67.s:
tataḥ karma cakārāsya tejaḥsaṃvarddhanaṃ mahat /
teṣāṃ ca buddhisaṃmohamakarodbuddhisattamaḥ //
2.67.d:
ततः कर्म चकारास्य तेजःसंवर्द्धनं महत् ।
तेषां च बुद्धिसंमोहमकरोद्बुद्धिसत्तमः ॥
2.67.m: Then that best of the intelligent performed a great rite to increase his radiance, / and caused delusion of mind in them.

2.67.s:
te yadā tu susaṃmūḍā rāgānmatto vidharmiṇaḥ /
brahmadviṣaśca saṃbṛttā hatavīryaparākramāḥ //
2.67.d:
ते यदा तु सुसंमूडा रागान्मत्तो विधर्मिणः ।
ब्रह्मद्विषश्च संबृत्ता हतवीर्यपराक्रमाः ॥
2.67.m: When they became completely deluded, maddened by passion, unrighteous, / and haters of brāhmaṇas, their strength and prowess destroyed,

2.67.s:
tato lebhe 'suraiśvaryamaindrasthānaṃ tathottamam /
hatvā rajisutānsarvānkāmakrodhaparāyaṇān //
2.67.d:
ततो लेभे ऽसुरैश्वर्यमैन्द्रस्थानं तथोत्तमम् ।
हत्वा रजिसुतान्सर्वान्कामक्रोधपरायणान् ॥
2.67.m: then, having slain all the sons of Raji devoted to lust and wrath, / he regained the sovereignty of the asuras and the supreme status of Indra.

2.67.s:
ya idaṃ cyavanaṃ sthānātpratiṣṭhāṃ ca śatakratoḥ /
śṛṇuyācchrāvayedvāpi na sa daurātmyamāpnuyāt //
iti śrībrahmāṇḍe mahāpurāṇe vāyuprokte madhyamabhāge tṛtīya upoddhātapāde dhanvantarisaṃbhavādivarṇanaṃ nāma saptaṣaṣṭitamo 'dhyāyaḥ // 67//
2.67.d:
य इदं च्यवनं स्थानात्प्रतिष्ठां च शतक्रतोः ।
शृणुयाच्छ्रावयेद्वापि न स दौरात्म्यमाप्नुयात् ॥
इति श्रीब्रह्माण्डे महापुराणे वायुप्रोक्ते मध्यमभागे तृतीय उपोद्धातपादे धन्वन्तरिसंभवादिवर्णनं नाम सप्तषष्टितमो ऽध्यायः ॥ 67॥
2.67.m:
Whoever hears or recites this fall from station and restoration of Śatakratu, / he shall never meet with wickedness.

Thus ends the sixty-seventh chapter, entitled “Description of the Origin of Dhanvantari and Others,” in the third [section], the Upoddhātapāda, in the middle part of the glorious and great Brahmāṇḍa Purāṇa proclaimed by Vāyu. // 67

2.68.s:
ṛṣaya ūcuḥ
marutena kathaṃ kanyā rājñe dattā mahātmanā /
kiṃvīryāśca mahātmāno jātā marutakanyayā //
2.68.d:
ऋषय ऊचुः
मरुतेन कथं कन्या राज्ञे दत्ता महात्मना ।
किंवीर्याश्च महात्मानो जाता मरुतकन्यया ॥
2.68.m: The sages said: / “How was a daughter given by the great-souled Marutta to the king? / And of what valour were the great-souled ones born of Marutta's daughter?”

2.68.s:
sūta uvāca
āharatsa marutsomamannakāmaḥ prajeśvaraḥ /
māsimāsi mahātejāḥ ṣaṣṭisaṃvatsarānnṛpa //
2.68.d:
सूत उवाच
आहरत्स मरुत्सोममन्नकामः प्रजेश्वरः ।
मासिमासि महातेजाः षष्टिसंवत्सरान्नृप ॥
2.68.m: The bard said: / “Desiring food, that lord of subjects, of great splendour, / performed the Marutsoma sacrifice month after month for sixty years, O king.

2.68.s:
tena te marutastasya marutsomena toṣitāḥ /
akṣayyānnaṃ daduḥ prītāḥ sarvakāmaparicchadam //
2.68.d:
तेन ते मरुतस्तस्य मरुत्सोमेन तोषिताः ।
अक्षय्यान्नं ददुः प्रीताः सर्वकामपरिच्छदम् ॥
2.68.m: Pleased with that Marutsoma of his, the Maruts / gave him inexhaustible food, accompanied by every object of desire.

2.68.s:
annaṃ tasya sakṛdbhuktamahorātraṃ na kṣīyate /
koṭiśo dīya mānaṃ ca sūryasyodayanādapi //
2.68.d:
अन्नं तस्य सकृद्भुक्तमहोरात्रं न क्षीयते ।
कोटिशो दीय मानं च सूर्यस्योदयनादपि ॥
2.68.m: Food of his, eaten once, was not depleted throughout day and night, / even when given by crores from the rising of the sun.

2.68.s:
mitrajyotestu kanyāyā maritasya ca dhīmataḥ /
tasmājjātā mahāsattvā dharmajñā mokṣadarśinaḥ //
2.68.d:
मित्रज्योतेस्तु कन्याया मरितस्य च धीमतः ।
तस्माज्जाता महासत्त्वा धर्मज्ञा मोक्षदर्शिनः ॥
2.68.m: From Mitrajyoti's daughter and the wise Marutta / were born those beings of great sattva, knowers of dharma, seers of liberation.

2.68.s:
saṃnyasya gṛhadharmāṇi vairāgyaṃ samupasthitāḥ /
yatidharmamavāpyeha brahmabhūyāya te gatāḥ //
2.68.d:
संन्यस्य गृहधर्माणि वैराग्यं समुपस्थिताः ।
यतिधर्ममवाप्येह ब्रह्मभूयाय ते गताः ॥
2.68.m: Renouncing household duties and attaining dispassion, / having undertaken the dharma of ascetics here, they went to absorption in Brahman.

2.68.s:
anenasaḥ suto jātaḥ kṣatradharmaḥ pratāpavān /
kṣatradharmasuto jātaḥ pratipakṣo mahātapāḥ //
2.68.d:
अनेनसः सुतो जातः क्षत्रधर्मः प्रतापवान् ।
क्षत्रधर्मसुतो जातः प्रतिपक्षो महातपाः ॥
2.68.m: To Anenas was born a son, the glorious Kṣatradharma. / The son of Kṣatradharma was Pratipakṣa, rich in austerities.

2.68.s:
pratipakṣasutaścāpi sṛṃjayo nāma viśrutaḥ /
sṛṃjayasya jayaḥ putro vijayastasya jajñivān //
2.68.d:
प्रतिपक्षसुतश्चापि सृंजयो नाम विश्रुतः ।
सृंजयस्य जयः पुत्रो विजयस्तस्य जज्ञिवान् ॥
2.68.m: The son of Pratipakṣa was renowned as Sṛñjaya. / The son of Sṛñjaya was Jaya; Vijaya was born to him.

2.68.s:
vijayasya jayaḥ putrastasya haryaśvakaḥ smṛtaḥ /
iryaśvasya suto rājā sahadevaḥ pratāpavān //
2.68.d:
विजयस्य जयः पुत्रस्तस्य हर्यश्वकः स्मृतः ।
इर्यश्वस्य सुतो राजा सहदेवः प्रतापवान् ॥
2.68.m: The son of Vijaya was Jaya; his [son] is remembered as Haryaśva. / The son of Haryaśva was the glorious king Sahadeva.

2.68.s:
sahadevasya dharmātmā ahīna iti viśrutaḥ /
ahīnasya cayatsenastasya putro 'tha saṃkṛtiḥ //
2.68.d:
सहदेवस्य धर्मात्मा अहीन इति विश्रुतः ।
अहीनस्य चयत्सेनस्तस्य पुत्रो ऽथ संकृतिः ॥
2.68.m: The righteous [son] of Sahadeva was renowned as Ahīna. / Ahīna's [son] was Jayatsena; then his son was Saṅkṛti.

2.68.s:
saṃkṛterapi dharmātmā kṛtadharmā mahāyaśāḥ /
ityete kṣatradharmāṇo nahuṣasya nibodhata //
2.68.d:
संकृतेरपि धर्मात्मा कृतधर्मा महायशाः ।
इत्येते क्षत्रधर्माणो नहुषस्य निबोधत ॥
2.68.m: The son of Saṅkṛti was the righteous, highly renowned Kṛtadharma. / These are the descendants of Kṣatradharma. Hear [now] of Nahuṣa.

2.68.s:
nahuṣasya tu dāyādāḥ ṣaḍindropamatejasaḥ /
yatiryayātiḥ saṃyātirāyatirviyatiḥ kṛtiḥ //
2.68.d:
नहुषस्य तु दायादाः षडिन्द्रोपमतेजसः ।
यतिर्ययातिः संयातिरायतिर्वियतिः कृतिः ॥
2.68.m: The heirs of Nahuṣa were six, equal in splendour to Indra: / Yati, Yayāti, Saṃyāti, Āyati, Viyati, and Kṛti.

2.68.s:
yatirjyeṣṭhastu teṣāṃ vai yayātistu tato 'varaḥ /
kākutsthakanyāṃ gāṃ nāma lebhe patnīṃ yatistadā //
2.68.d:
यतिर्ज्येष्ठस्तु तेषां वै ययातिस्तु ततो ऽवरः ।
काकुत्स्थकन्यां गां नाम लेभे पत्नीं यतिस्तदा ॥
2.68.m: Yati was indeed the eldest of them, and Yayāti was younger than he. / At that time Yati obtained the daughter of Kakutstha, named Go, as his wife.

2.68.s:
sa yatirmokṣamāsthāya brahmabhūto 'bhavanmuniḥ /
teṣāṃ madhye tu pañcānāṃ yayātiḥ pṛthivīpatiḥ //
2.68.d:
स यतिर्मोक्षमास्थाय ब्रह्मभूतो ऽभवन्मुनिः ।
तेषां मध्ये तु पञ्चानां ययातिः पृथिवीपतिः ॥
2.68.m: Taking recourse in liberation, that sage Yati became identified with Brahman. / But among those five, Yayāti became the lord of the earth.

2.68.s:
devayānīmuśanasaḥ sutāṃ bhāryāmavāpa ha /
śarmiṣṭhāmāsurīṃ caiva tanayāṃ vṛṣaparvaṇaḥ //
2.68.d:
देवयानीमुशनसः सुतां भार्यामवाप ह ।
शर्मिष्ठामासुरीं चैव तनयां वृषपर्वणः ॥
2.68.m: He obtained Devayānī, the daughter of Uśanas, as his wife, / and also Śarmiṣṭhā the Asura woman, the daughter of Vṛṣaparvan.

2.68.s:
yaduṃ ca turvasuṃ caiva devayāno vyajāyata /
druhyuṃ cānuṃ ca pūruṃ ca śarmiṣṭhā vārṣaparvaṇī //
2.68.d:
यदुं च तुर्वसुं चैव देवयानो व्यजायत ।
द्रुह्युं चानुं च पूरुं च शर्मिष्ठा वार्षपर्वणी ॥
2.68.m: Devayānī gave birth to Yadu and Turvasu, / and Śarmiṣṭhā, daughter of Vṛṣaparvan, [gave birth to] Druhyu, Anu, and Pūru.

2.68.s:
ajījananmahāvīryānsutāndevasutopamān /
rathaṃ tasmai dadau śakraḥ prītaḥ paramabhāsvaram //
2.68.d:
अजीजनन्महावीर्यान्सुतान्देवसुतोपमान् ।
रथं तस्मै ददौ शक्रः प्रीतः परमभास्वरम् ॥
2.68.m: She gave birth to sons of great valor, equal to the sons of the gods. / Pleased, Śakra gave him an exceedingly radiant chariot,

2.68.s:
asaṃgaṃ kāñcanaṃ divyamakṣayau ca maheṣudhī /
yuktaṃ manojavairaśvairyena kanyāṃ samudvahat //
2.68.d:
असंगं काञ्चनं दिव्यमक्षयौ च महेषुधी ।
युक्तं मनोजवैरश्वैर्येन कन्यां समुद्वहत् ॥
2.68.m: unimpeded, golden, divine, with two inexhaustible large quivers, / yoked with horses swift as thought, by means of which he carried off his bride.

2.68.s:
sa tena rathamukhyena jigāya satataṃ mahīm /
yayātiryudhi durddharṣo devadānavamānavaiḥ //
2.68.d:
स तेन रथमुख्येन जिगाय सततं महीम् ।
ययातिर्युधि दुर्द्धर्षो देवदानवमानवैः ॥
2.68.m: By means of that foremost chariot, he continually conquered the earth— / Yayāti, invincible in battle by gods, Dānavas, and human beings.

2.68.s:
pauravāṇāṃ nṛpāṇāṃ ca sarveṣāṃ so 'bhavadrathī /
yāvatsudeśaprabhavaḥ kauravo janamejayaḥ //
2.68.d:
पौरवाणां नृपाणां च सर्वेषां सो ऽभवद्रथी ।
यावत्सुदेशप्रभवः कौरवो जनमेजयः ॥
2.68.m: And he was the charioteer [i.e., possessor of that chariot] among all the Paurava kings, / until the Kaurava Janamejaya, born of Sudeṣṇā.

2.68.s:
kuroḥ pautrasya rājñaratu rājñaḥ pārīkṣitasya ha /
jagāma saratho nāśaṃ śāpādgārgyasya dhīmataḥ //
2.68.d:
कुरोः पौत्रस्य राज्ञरतु राज्ञः पारीक्षितस्य ह ।
जगाम सरथो नाशं शापाद्गार्ग्यस्य धीमतः ॥
2.68.m: Due to the curse of the wise Gārgya, that chariot went to destruction / in the time of that king, the grandson of Kuru, the son of Parīkṣit.

2.68.s:
gārgyasya hi sutaṃ bālaṃ sa rājā janamejayaḥ /
durbuddhirhiṃsayā māsa lohagandhī narādhipaḥ //
2.68.d:
गार्ग्यस्य हि सुतं बालं स राजा जनमेजयः ।
दुर्बुद्धिर्हिंसया मास लोहगन्धी नराधिपः ॥
2.68.m: For that evil-minded king Janamejaya, ruler of men, / killed the young son of Gārgya and became smelling of iron.

2.68.s:
sa lohagandhī rājarṣiḥ paridhāvannitastataḥ /
paurajānapadaistyakto na lebhe śarma karhicit //
2.68.d:
स लोहगन्धी राजर्षिः परिधावन्नितस्ततः ।
पौरजानपदैस्त्यक्तो न लेभे शर्म कर्हिचित् ॥
2.68.m: That royal sage, smelling of iron, running about hither and thither, / abandoned by citizens and country-folk, found no peace anywhere.

2.68.s:
tataḥ sa duḥkhasaṃtapto nālabhatsaṃvidaṃ kvacita /
sa prāyācchaunakamṛṣiṃ śaraṇaṃ vyathitastadā //
2.68.d:
ततः स दुःखसंतप्तो नालभत्संविदं क्वचित ।
स प्रायाच्छौनकमृषिं शरणं व्यथितस्तदा ॥
2.68.m: Then, tormented by sorrow, he found no consciousness anywhere; / afflicted, he then went to the sage Śaunaka for refuge.

2.68.s:
indrotonāma vikhyāto yo 'sau muni rudāradhīḥ /
yojayāmāsa caindrotaḥ śaunako janamejayam //
2.68.d:
इन्द्रोतोनाम विख्यातो यो ऽसौ मुनि रुदारधीः ।
योजयामास चैन्द्रोतः शौनको जनमेजयम् ॥
2.68.m: That noble-minded sage was renowned by the name Indrota; / and Indrota Śaunaka engaged Janamejaya,

2.68.s:
aśvamedhena rājānaṃ pāvanārthaṃ dvijottamāḥ /
sa lohagandho vyanaśatta syāvabhṛthametya ha //
2.68.d:
अश्वमेधेन राजानं पावनार्थं द्विजोत्तमाः ।
स लोहगन्धो व्यनशत्त स्यावभृथमेत्य ह ॥
2.68.m: the king, in a horse sacrifice for purification, O best of the twice-born. / That smell of iron vanished upon his reaching the concluding bath.

2.68.s:
sa vai divyo rathastasmādvasoścedipatestathā /
dattaḥ śakrena tuṣṭena lebhe tasmādbṛhadrathaḥ //
2.68.d:
स वै दिव्यो रथस्तस्माद्वसोश्चेदिपतेस्तथा ।
दत्तः शक्रेन तुष्टेन लेभे तस्माद्बृहद्रथः ॥
2.68.m: That divine chariot was given by the pleased Śakra / to Vasu, the lord of Cedi, and from him Bṛhadratha obtained it.

2.68.s:
tato hatvā jarāsaṃdhaṃ bhīmastaṃ rathamuttamam /
pradadau vāsudevāya prītyā kauravanandanaḥ //
2.68.d:
ततो हत्वा जरासंधं भीमस्तं रथमुत्तमम् ।
प्रददौ वासुदेवाय प्रीत्या कौरवनन्दनः ॥
2.68.m: Then, having slain Jarāsaṃdha, Bhīma, the delighter of the Kurus, / affectionately gave that excellent chariot to Vāsudeva.

2.68.s:
sa jarāṃ prāpya rājarṣiryayātirnahuṣātmajaḥ /
putraṃ śreṣṭaṃ variṣṭhaṃ ca yadumityabravīdvacaḥ //
2.68.d:
स जरां प्राप्य राजर्षिर्ययातिर्नहुषात्मजः ।
पुत्रं श्रेष्टं वरिष्ठं च यदुमित्यब्रवीद्वचः ॥
2.68.m: Having reached old age, that royal sage Yayāti, son of Nahuṣa, / spoke these words to his eldest and foremost son, Yadu:

2.68.s:
jarāvalī ca māṃ tāta palitāni ca paryayuḥ /
kāvyasyośanasaḥ śāpānna ca tṛpto 'smi yauvane //
2.68.d:
जरावली च मां तात पलितानि च पर्ययुः ।
काव्यस्योशनसः शापान्न च तृप्तो ऽस्मि यौवने ॥
2.68.m: “O dear one, old age, wrinkles, and grey hairs have overcome me / by the curse of Kāvya Uśanas, and I am not yet satiated with youth.

2.68.s:
tvaṃ yado pratipadyasva pāpmānaṃ jarayā saha /
jarāṃ me pratigṛhṇīṣva taṃ yaduḥ pratyuvāca ha //
2.68.d:
त्वं यदो प्रतिपद्यस्व पाप्मानं जरया सह ।
जरां मे प्रतिगृह्णीष्व तं यदुः प्रत्युवाच ह ॥
2.68.m: You, O Yadu, take on this evil together with old age; / receive my old age.” To him Yadu replied:

2.68.s:
anirdiṣṭā hi me bhikṣā brāhmaṇasya pratiśrutā /
sā tu vyāyāmasādhyā vai na grahīṣyāmi te jarām //
2.68.d:
अनिर्दिष्टा हि मे भिक्षा ब्राह्मणस्य प्रतिश्रुता ।
सा तु व्यायामसाध्या वै न ग्रहीष्यामि ते जराम् ॥
2.68.m: “Alms have been promised by me, unspecified, to a brāhmaṇa, / but that can only be accomplished through physical exertion; I will not take your old age.

2.68.s:
jarāyāṃ bahavo doṣāḥ pānabhojanakāritāḥ /
tasmājjarāṃ na te rājangrahītumahamutsahe //
2.68.d:
जरायां बहवो दोषाः पानभोजनकारिताः ।
तस्माज्जरां न ते राजन्ग्रहीतुमहमुत्सहे ॥
2.68.m: In old age there are many afflictions caused by eating and drinking; / therefore, O king, I cannot bear to take your old age.

2.68.s:
sitaśmaśrudharo dīno jarayā śithilīkṛtaḥ /
valīsaṃtatagātraśca nirāśo durbalākṛtiḥ //
2.68.d:
सितश्मश्रुधरो दीनो जरया शिथिलीकृतः ।
वलीसंततगात्रश्च निराशो दुर्बलाकृतिः ॥
2.68.m: Wearing a white beard, wretched, made slack by old age, / with limbs covered in wrinkles, hopeless, of feeble appearance,

2.68.s:
aśaktaḥ kāryakaraṇe paribūtastu yauvane /
sahopavītibhiścaiva tāṃ jarāṃ nābhikāmaye //
2.68.d:
अशक्तः कार्यकरणे परिबूतस्तु यौवने ।
सहोपवीतिभिश्चैव तां जरां नाभिकामये ॥
2.68.m: incapable of performing actions, disgraced in the prime of youth / even by those wearing sacred threads—I do not desire that old age.

2.68.s:
saṃti te bahavaḥ putrā mattaḥ priyatarā nṛpa /
pratigṛhṇantu dharmajña putramanyaṃ vṛṇīṣva vai //
2.68.d:
संति ते बहवः पुत्रा मत्तः प्रियतरा नृप ।
प्रतिगृह्णन्तु धर्मज्ञ पुत्रमन्यं वृणीष्व वै ॥
2.68.m: You have many sons dearer than me, O king. / Let them accept it, O knower of dharma; choose another son!”

2.68.s:
sa evamukto yadunā dīvrakopasamanvitaḥ /
uvāca vadatāṃ śreṣṭo jyeṣṭhaṃ taṃ garhayansutam //
2.68.d:
स एवमुक्तो यदुना दीव्रकोपसमन्वितः ।
उवाच वदतां श्रेष्टो ज्येष्ठं तं गर्हयन्सुतम् ॥
2.68.m: Addressed thus by Yadu, filled with intense anger, / that best of speakers spoke, rebuking his eldest son:

2.68.s:
āśramaḥ kastavānyo 'sti ko vā dharmavidhistava /
māmanādṛtya durbuddhe yadahaṃ tava deśikaḥ //
2.68.d:
आश्रमः कस्तवान्यो ऽस्ति को वा धर्मविधिस्तव ।
मामनादृत्य दुर्बुद्धे यदहं तव देशिकः ॥
2.68.m: “What other stage of life is yours, or what rule of duty is yours, / disregarding me, O evil-minded one, when I am your teacher?

2.68.s:
evamuktvā yaduṃ rājā śaśāpainaṃ sa manyumān /
yastvaṃ me tdṛdayājjāto vayaḥ svaṃ na prayacchasi //
2.68.d:
एवमुक्त्वा यदुं राजा शशापैनं स मन्युमान् ।
यस्त्वं मे त्दृदयाज्जातो वयः स्वं न प्रयच्छसि ॥
2.68.m: Having spoken thus to Yadu, the enraged king cursed him: / ‘Because you, born from my heart, do not give your youth,

2.68.s:
tasmānna rājyabhāṅmūḍha prajā te vai bhaviṣyati /
turvaso pratipadyasva pāpmānaṃ jarayā saha //
2.68.d:
तस्मान्न राज्यभाङ्मूढ प्रजा ते वै भविष्यति ।
तुर्वसो प्रतिपद्यस्व पाप्मानं जरया सह ॥
2.68.m: therefore, O fool, your offspring shall not possess a kingdom!’ / ‘Turvasu, take on this evil together with old age!’”

2.68.s:
turvasuruvāca
na kāmaye jarāṃ tāta kāmabhogapraṇāśinīm /
jarāyāṃ bahavo doṣāḥ pānabhojana kāritāḥ //
2.68.d:
तुर्वसुरुवाच
न कामये जरां तात कामभोगप्रणाशिनीम् ।
जरायां बहवो दोषाः पानभोजन कारिताः ॥
2.68.m: Turvasu said: / “O father, I do not desire old age, which destroys desires and pleasures. / In old age there are many afflictions caused by eating and drinking;

2.68.s:
tasmājjarāṃ na te rājangrahītumahamutsahe /
yayātiruvāca
yastvaṃ me tdṛdayājjāto vayaḥ svaṃ na prayacchasi //
2.68.d:
तस्माज्जरां न ते राजन्ग्रहीतुमहमुत्सहे ।
ययातिरुवाच
यस्त्वं मे त्दृदयाज्जातो वयः स्वं न प्रयच्छसि ॥
2.68.m: therefore, O king, I cannot bear to take your old age.” / Yayāti said: / “Because you, born from my heart, do not give your youth,

2.68.s:
tasmātprajānu vicchedaṃ turvaso tava yāsyati /
saṃkīrṇeṣu ca dharmeṇa pratilomanareṣu ca //
2.68.d:
तस्मात्प्रजानु विच्छेदं तुर्वसो तव यास्यति ।
संकीर्णेषु च धर्मेण प्रतिलोमनरेषु च ॥
2.68.m: therefore, O Turvasu, your offspring will go to ruin / among those of mixed duty and men born of Pratiloma unions,

2.68.s:
piśitāśiṣu cānyeṣu mūḍha rājā bhaviṣyasi /
gurudāraprasakteṣu tiryagyonigateṣu vā /
vāsaste pāpa mleccheṣu bhaviṣyati na saṃśayaḥ //
2.68.d:
पिशिताशिषु चान्येषु मूढ राजा भविष्यसि ।
गुरुदारप्रसक्तेषु तिर्यग्योनिगतेषु वा ।
वासस्ते पाप म्लेच्छेषु भविष्यति न संशयः ॥
2.68.m: and among other meat-eaters, O fool, you shall be king; / among those devoted to the wives of gurus or those descended into animal wombs, / your dwelling, O evil one, will be among the Mlecchas, there is no doubt.”

2.68.s:
sūta uvāca
evaṃ tu turvasuṃśaptvā yayātiḥ sutamātmanaḥ //
2.68.d:
सूत उवाच
एवं तु तुर्वसुंशप्त्वा ययातिः सुतमात्मनः ॥
2.68.m: The bard said: / Having cursed his son Turvasu thus,

2.68.s:
śarmiṣṭhāyāḥ sutaṃ druhyumidaṃ vacanamabravīt /
druhyo tvaṃ pratipadyasva varṇarūpavināśinīm //
2.68.d:
शर्मिष्ठायाः सुतं द्रुह्युमिदं वचनमब्रवीत् ।
द्रुह्यो त्वं प्रतिपद्यस्व वर्णरूपविनाशिनीम् ॥
2.68.m: Yayāti spoke these words to Druhyu, son of Śarmiṣṭhā: / “O Druhyu, take on [this old age] that destroys color and beauty,

2.68.s:
jarā varṣasahasraṃvai yauvanaṃ svaṃ dadasva me /
pūrṇe varṣasahasre te pratidāsyāmi yauvanam //
2.68.d:
जरा वर्षसहस्रंवै यौवनं स्वं ददस्व मे ।
पूर्णे वर्षसहस्रे ते प्रतिदास्यामि यौवनम् ॥
2.68.m: old age for a thousand years; give your youth to me! / When a thousand years are completed, I will give you back your youth,

2.68.s:
svaṃ cādāsyāmi bhūyo 'haṃ pāpmānaṃ jarayā saha /
druhyuruvāca
nāroheta rathaṃ nāśvaṃ jīrṇo bhuṅkte na ca striyam /
na sukhaṃ cāsya bhavati na jarāṃ tena kāmaye //
2.68.d:
स्वं चादास्यामि भूयो ऽहं पाप्मानं जरया सह ।
द्रुह्युरुवाच
नारोहेत रथं नाश्वं जीर्णो भुङ्क्ते न च स्त्रियम् ।
न सुखं चास्य भवति न जरां तेन कामये ॥
2.68.m: and I will take back my own evil along with old age.” / Druhyu said: / “An old man cannot mount a chariot or a horse, nor enjoy a woman; / he has no pleasure; therefore I do not desire old age.”

2.68.s:
yayātiruvāca
yastvaṃ me hṛdayājjāto vayaḥ svaṃ na prayacchasi //
2.68.d:
ययातिरुवाच
यस्त्वं मे हृदयाज्जातो वयः स्वं न प्रयच्छसि ॥
2.68.m: Yayāti said: / “Because you, born from my heart, do not give your youth,

2.68.s:
tasmāddruhyo priyaḥ kāmo na te saṃpatsyate kvacit /
nauplavottarasaṃcārastava nityaṃ bhaviṣyati //
2.68.d:
तस्माद्द्रुह्यो प्रियः कामो न ते संपत्स्यते क्वचित् ।
नौप्लवोत्तरसंचारस्तव नित्यं भविष्यति ॥
2.68.m: therefore, O Druhyu, your beloved desire will never be fulfilled; / your perpetual movement will be over water by boat.

2.68.s:
arājā rājavaṃśastvaṃ tatra nityaṃ vasiṣyasi /
ano tvaṃ pratipādyasva pāpmānaṃ jarayā saha //
2.68.d:
अराजा राजवंशस्त्वं तत्र नित्यं वसिष्यसि ।
अनो त्वं प्रतिपाद्यस्व पाप्मानं जरया सह ॥
2.68.m: You of royal lineage shall not be a king, and there you shall always dwell. / Anu, take on this evil together with old age,

2.68.s:
evaṃ varṣasahasraṃ tu careyaṃ yauvanena te /
anuruvāca
jīrṇaḥ śiśurivāśakto jarayā hyaśuciḥ sadā /
na juhoti sa kāle 'gniṃ tāṃ jarāṃ nābhikāmaye //
2.68.d:
एवं वर्षसहस्रं तु चरेयं यौवनेन ते ।
अनुरुवाच
जीर्णः शिशुरिवाशक्तो जरया ह्यशुचिः सदा ।
न जुहोति स काले ऽग्निं तां जरां नाभिकामये ॥
2.68.m: so that I may enjoy for a thousand years with your youth.” / Anu said: / “An old man, like a helpless child, is ever unclean on account of old age; / he does not offer into the fire at the proper time; I do not desire that old age.”

2.68.s:
yayātirūvāca /
yastvaṃ me hṛdayājjāto vayaḥ svaṃ na prayacchasi //
2.68.d:
ययातिरूवाच ।
यस्त्वं मे हृदयाज्जातो वयः स्वं न प्रयच्छसि ॥
2.68.m: Yayāti said: / “Because you, born from my heart, do not give your youth,

2.68.s:
jarādoṣa stvayokto 'yaṃ tasmāttvaṃ pratipatsyase /
prajā ca yauvanaṃ prāptā vinaśiṣyatyano tava //
2.68.d:
जरादोष स्त्वयोक्तो ऽयं तस्मात्त्वं प्रतिपत्स्यसे ।
प्रजा च यौवनं प्राप्ता विनशिष्यत्यनो तव ॥
2.68.m: and this fault of old age was spoken by you, therefore you shall experience it! / And your offspring, having reached youth, shall perish, O Anu;

2.68.s:
agnipraskandanaparāstvaṃ vāpyevaṃ bhaviṣyasi /
pūro tvaṃ pratipadyasva pāpmānaṃ jarayā saha //
2.68.d:
अग्निप्रस्कन्दनपरास्त्वं वाप्येवं भविष्यसि ।
पूरो त्वं प्रतिपद्यस्व पाप्मानं जरया सह ॥
2.68.m: and you too shall be one whose habit is neglecting the sacred fire! / Pūru, take on this evil together with old age!

2.68.s:
jarāvalī ca māṃ tāta palitāni ca paryayuḥ /
kāvyasyośanasaḥ śāpānna ca tṛpto 'smiyauvane //
2.68.d:
जरावली च मां तात पलितानि च पर्ययुः ।
काव्यस्योशनसः शापान्न च तृप्तो ऽस्मियौवने ॥
2.68.m: O dear one, old age, wrinkles, and grey hairs have overcome me / by the curse of Kāvya Uśanas, and I am not yet satiated with youth.

2.68.s:
kañcitkālaṃ careyaṃ vai viṣayānvayasā tava /
pūrṇe varṣasahasre te pratidāsyāmi yauvanam //
2.68.d:
कञ्चित्कालं चरेयं वै विषयान्वयसा तव ।
पूर्णे वर्षसहस्रे ते प्रतिदास्यामि यौवनम् ॥
2.68.m: I would wander among sense objects for some time with your youth; / when a thousand years are completed, I will give you back your youth,

2.68.s:
svaṃ caiva pratipatsye 'haṃ pāpmānaṃ jarayā saha /
sūta uvāca
evamuktaḥ pratyuvāca putraḥ pitaramañjasā //
2.68.d:
स्वं चैव प्रतिपत्स्ये ऽहं पाप्मानं जरया सह ।
सूत उवाच
एवमुक्तः प्रत्युवाच पुत्रः पितरमञ्जसा ॥
2.68.m: and I shall take back my own evil along with old age.” / The bard said: / Addressed thus, the son readily replied to his father:

2.68.s:
yathā tu manyase tāta kariṣyāmi tathaiva ca /
pratipatsye ca te rājanpāpmānaṃ jarayā saha //
2.68.d:
यथा तु मन्यसे तात करिष्यामि तथैव च ।
प्रतिपत्स्ये च ते राजन्पाप्मानं जरया सह ॥
2.68.m: “Just as you think, O father, so will I do; / and, O king, I will take on your evil together with old age.”

2.68.s:
gṛhāṇa yauvanaṃ mattaścara kāmānyathepsitān /
jarayāhaṃ praticchanno vayorūpadharastava //
2.68.d:
गृहाण यौवनं मत्तश्चर कामान्यथेप्सितान् ।
जरयाहं प्रतिच्छन्नो वयोरूपधरस्तव ॥
2.68.m: "Receive [my] youth from me, and pursue desired pleasures as you wish. / Concealed by [your] old age, bearing your age and form,

2.68.s:
yauvanaṃ bhavate dattvā cariṣyāmi yathārthavat /
yayātiruvāca
pūro prīto 'smi bhadraṃ te prītaścedaṃ dadāmi te //
2.68.d:
यौवनं भवते दत्त्वा चरिष्यामि यथार्थवत् ।
ययातिरुवाच
पूरो प्रीतो ऽस्मि भद्रं ते प्रीतश्चेदं ददामि ते ॥
2.68.m: having given [my] youth to you, I shall conduct myself properly." / Yayāti said: / "O Pūru, I am pleased; hail to you! Pleased, I grant you this:

2.68.s:
sarvakāmasamṛddhā te prajā rājye bhaviṣyati /
sūta uvāca
pūroranumato rājā yayātiḥ svajarāṃ tataḥ //
2.68.d:
सर्वकामसमृद्धा ते प्रजा राज्ये भविष्यति ।
सूत उवाच
पूरोरनुमतो राजा ययातिः स्वजरां ततः ॥
2.68.m: Your subjects in the kingdom shall abound in all desires." / The bard said: / Permitted by Pūru, King Yayāti then transferred his old age,

2.68.s:
saṃkrāmayāmāsa tadā prāsādadbhārgavasya tu /
gauraveṇātha vayasā yayātirnahuṣātmajaḥ //
2.68.d:
संक्रामयामास तदा प्रासादद्भार्गवस्य तु ।
गौरवेणाथ वयसा ययातिर्नहुषात्मजः ॥
2.68.m: by the grace of Bhārgava. / With dignity and [youthful] age, Yayāti, the son of Nahuṣa,

2.68.s:
prītiyukto naraśreṣṭhaścacāra viṣayānsvakān /
yathākāmaṃ yathotsāhaṃ yathākālaṃ yathāsukham //
2.68.d:
प्रीतियुक्तो नरश्रेष्ठश्चचार विषयान्स्वकान् ।
यथाकामं यथोत्साहं यथाकालं यथासुखम् ॥
2.68.m: filled with joy, best among men, enjoyed his realms / according to desire, according to energy, according to time, and according to pleasure.

2.68.s:
dharmāvirodhī rājendro yathāśakti sa eva hi /
devānatarpayadyajñaiḥ pitṝñśrāddhaistathaiva ca //
2.68.d:
धर्माविरोधी राजेन्द्रो यथाशक्ति स एव हि ।
देवानतर्पयद्यज्ञैः पितॄञ्श्राद्धैस्तथैव च ॥
2.68.m: Not conflicting with righteousness, that emperor indeed according to his ability / gratified the gods with sacrifices and likewise the ancestors with śrāddhas,

2.68.s:
dārānanugrahairiṣṭaiḥ kāmaiśca dvijasattamān /
atithīnannapānaiśca vaiśyaṃśca paripālanaiḥ //
2.68.d:
दाराननुग्रहैरिष्टैः कामैश्च द्विजसत्तमान् ।
अतिथीनन्नपानैश्च वैश्यंश्च परिपालनैः ॥
2.68.m: his wives with cherished kindnesses, the best of the twice-born with desires, / guests with food and drink, and Vaiśyas through protection,

2.68.s:
ānṛśaṃsyena śūdrāṃśca dasyūnsaṃnigraheṇa ca /
dharmeṇa ca prajāḥ sarvā yathāvadanurañjayat //
2.68.d:
आनृशंस्येन शूद्रांश्च दस्यून्संनिग्रहेण च ।
धर्मेण च प्रजाः सर्वा यथावदनुरञ्जयत् ॥
2.68.m: Śūdras with kindliness, and brigands with restraint; / and by righteousness he delighted all the subjects properly.

2.68.s:
yayātiḥ pālayāmāsa sākṣādindra ivāparaḥ /
sa rājā siṃhavikrānto yuvā viṣayagocaraḥ //
2.68.d:
ययातिः पालयामास साक्षादिन्द्र इवापरः ।
स राजा सिंहविक्रान्तो युवा विषयगोचरः ॥
2.68.m: Yayāti ruled like a second Indra in visible form. / That king, with the prowess of a lion, young, dwelling in the sphere of sense-objects,

2.68.s:
avirodhena dharmasya cacāra sukhamuttamam /
sa mārgamāṇaḥ kāmānāmataddoṣanidarśanāt //
2.68.d:
अविरोधेन धर्मस्य चचार सुखमुत्तमम् ।
स मार्गमाणः कामानामतद्दोषनिदर्शनात् ॥
2.68.m: enjoyed supreme pleasure without contradicting righteousness. / Seeking pleasures because of not perceiving fault in them,

2.68.s:
viśvācyā sahito reme vaibrāje nandane vane /
apaśyatsa yadā tānvai varddhamānānnṛpastadā //
2.68.d:
विश्वाच्या सहितो रेमे वैब्राजे नन्दने वने ।
अपश्यत्स यदा तान्वै वर्द्धमानान्नृपस्तदा ॥
2.68.m: he took delight together with Viśvācī in the Vaibrāja and Nandana groves. / When that king saw those [desires] ever-increasing,

2.68.s:
gatvā pūroḥ sakāśaṃ vai svāṃ jarāṃ pratyapadyata /
saṃprāpya sa tu tānkāmāṃstṛptaḥ khinnaśca pārthivaḥ //
2.68.d:
गत्वा पूरोः सकाशं वै स्वां जरां प्रत्यपद्यत ।
संप्राप्य स तु तान्कामांस्तृप्तः खिन्नश्च पार्थिवः ॥
2.68.m: then going into the presence of Pūru, he took back his own old age. / Having obtained those desires, the king was satiated and weary.

2.68.s:
kālaṃ varṣasahasraṃ vai sasmāra manujādhipaḥ /
parisaṃkhyāya kāle ca kalāḥ kāṣṭhāstathaiva ca //
2.68.d:
कालं वर्षसहस्रं वै सस्मार मनुजाधिपः ।
परिसंख्याय काले च कलाः काष्ठास्तथैव च ॥
2.68.m: The lord of men remembered the time of a thousand years; / and calculating the time in kalās and kāṣṭhās,

2.68.s:
pūrṇaṃ matvā tataḥ kālaṃ pūruṃ putramuvāca ha /
yathā sukhaṃ yathotsāhaṃ yathākālamarindama //
2.68.d:
पूर्णं मत्वा ततः कालं पूरुं पुत्रमुवाच ह ।
यथा सुखं यथोत्साहं यथाकालमरिन्दम ॥
2.68.m: considering the time complete, he said to his son Pūru: / "According to pleasure, according to energy, according to time, O subduer of enemies,

2.68.s:
sevitā viṣayaḥ putra yauvanena mayā tava /
pūro prīto 'smi bhadraṃ te gṛhāṇa tvaṃ svayauvanam //
2.68.d:
सेविता विषयः पुत्र यौवनेन मया तव ।
पूरो प्रीतो ऽस्मि भद्रं ते गृहाण त्वं स्वयौवनम् ॥
2.68.m: the realms [of pleasure] have been enjoyed by me, son, with your youth. / O Pūru, I am pleased; hail to you! Take your youth,

2.68.s:
rājyaṃ ca tvaṃ gṛhāṇedaṃ tvaṃ hi me priyakṛtsutaḥ /
pratipede jarāṃ rājā yayātirnahuṣātmajaḥ //
2.68.d:
राज्यं च त्वं गृहाणेदं त्वं हि मे प्रियकृत्सुतः ।
प्रतिपेदे जरां राजा ययातिर्नहुषात्मजः ॥
2.68.m: and receive this kingdom; for you are the son who did what was pleasing to me." / King Yayāti, son of Nahuṣa, received old age,

2.68.s:
yauvanaṃ pratipede ca pūruḥ svaṃ punarātmanaḥ /
abhiṣektukāmaṃ ca nṛpaṃ pūruṃ putraṃ kanīyasam //
2.68.d:
यौवनं प्रतिपेदे च पूरुः स्वं पुनरात्मनः ।
अभिषेक्तुकामं च नृपं पूरुं पुत्रं कनीयसम् ॥
2.68.m: and Pūru received back his own youth. / And when the king wished to consecrate his youngest son Pūru,

2.68.s:
brāhmaṇapramukhā varṇā idaṃ vacanamabruvan /
kathaṃ śukrasya naptāraṃ devayānyāḥ sutaṃ prabho //
2.68.d:
ब्राह्मणप्रमुखा वर्णा इदं वचनमब्रुवन् ।
कथं शुक्रस्य नप्तारं देवयान्याः सुतं प्रभो ॥
2.68.m: the castes headed by the Brāhmaṇas spoke these words: / "How, O lord, passing over the grandson of Śukra, the son of Devayānī,

2.68.s:
jyeṣṭhaṃ yadumatikramya rājyaṃ dāsyasi pūrave /
yadurjyeṣṭhastava suto jātastamanudaturvasuḥ //
2.68.d:
ज्येष्ठं यदुमतिक्रम्य राज्यं दास्यसि पूरवे ।
यदुर्ज्येष्ठस्तव सुतो जातस्तमनुदतुर्वसुः ॥
2.68.m: the eldest, Yadu, will you grant the kingdom to Pūru? / Yadu is your eldest son born, and Turvasu was born after him;

2.68.s:
śarmiṣṭhāyāḥ suto druhyustato 'nuḥ pūrureva ca /
kathaṃ jyeṣṭhānatikramya kanīyānrājyamarhati /
sutaḥ saṃbodhayāmastvāṃ dharmaṃ samanupālaya //
2.68.d:
शर्मिष्ठायाः सुतो द्रुह्युस्ततो ऽनुः पूरुरेव च ।
कथं ज्येष्ठानतिक्रम्य कनीयान्राज्यमर्हति ।
सुतः संबोधयामस्त्वां धर्मं समनुपालय ॥
2.68.m: Druhyu is the son of Śarmiṣṭhā, after him Anu, and then Pūru. / How does the youngest deserve the kingdom, passing over the elder ones? / We remind you, son; protect righteousness!"

2.68.s:
yayātiruvāca
brāhmaṇapramukhā varṇāḥ sarve śṛṇvantu me vacaḥ //
2.68.d:
ययातिरुवाच
ब्राह्मणप्रमुखा वर्णाः सर्वे शृण्वन्तु मे वचः ॥
2.68.m: Yayāti said: / "Let all the castes headed by the Brāhmaṇas hear my word,

2.68.s:
jyeṣṭhaṃ prati yathā rājyaṃ na deyaṃ me kathañcana /
mātāpitrorvacanakṛdvīraḥ putraḥ praśasyate //
2.68.d:
ज्येष्ठं प्रति यथा राज्यं न देयं मे कथञ्चन ।
मातापित्रोर्वचनकृद्वीरः पुत्रः प्रशस्यते ॥
2.68.m: as to why the kingdom is by no means to be given by me to the eldest: / A brave son who obeys the command of his mother and father is praised.

2.68.s:
mama jyeṣṭhena yadunā niyogo nānupālitaḥ /
pratikūlaḥ pituryaśca na sa putraḥ satāṃmataḥ //
2.68.d:
मम ज्येष्ठेन यदुना नियोगो नानुपालितः ।
प्रतिकूलः पितुर्यश्च न स पुत्रः सतांमतः ॥
2.68.m: My command was not obeyed by my eldest, Yadu; / and he who opposes his father is not regarded as a son by the virtuous.

2.68.s:
sa putraḥ putravadyaśca varttate pitṛmātṛṣu /
yadunāhamavajñātastathā turvasunāpi ca //
2.68.d:
स पुत्रः पुत्रवद्यश्च वर्त्तते पितृमातृषु ।
यदुनाहमवज्ञातस्तथा तुर्वसुनापि च ॥
2.68.m: He is a son who behaves like a son toward his father and mother. / I was disdained by Yadu, and likewise by Turvasu,

2.68.s:
druhyunā cānunā caiva mayyavajñā kṛtā bhṛśam /
pūruṇā tu kṛtaṃ vākyaṃ mānitaśca viśeṣataḥ //
2.68.d:
द्रुह्युना चानुना चैव मय्यवज्ञा कृता भृशम् ।
पूरुणा तु कृतं वाक्यं मानितश्च विशेषतः ॥
2.68.m: and severe disrespect toward me was shown by Druhyu and Anu. / But by Pūru my word was fulfilled, and I was honored especially;

2.68.s:
kanīyānmama dāyādo jarā yena dhṛtā mama /
sarve kāmā mama kṛtāḥ pūruṇā puṇyakāriṇā //
2.68.d:
कनीयान्मम दायादो जरा येन धृता मम ।
सर्वे कामा मम कृताः पूरुणा पुण्यकारिणा ॥
2.68.m: my younger son is the heir by whom my old age was taken. / All my desires were fulfilled by Pūru, the performer of virtuous deeds.

2.68.s:
śukreṇa ca varo dattaḥ kāvyenośanasā svayam /
putro yastvānuvartteta sa rājā tu mahāmate //
2.68.d:
शुक्रेण च वरो दत्तः काव्येनोशनसा स्वयम् ।
पुत्रो यस्त्वानुवर्त्तेत स राजा तु महामते ॥
2.68.m: And a boon was granted by Śukra, Kāvya Uśanas, himself: / 'The son who follows your will, O highly intelligent one, he shall indeed be king.'"

2.68.s:
prajā ūcuḥ
bhavato 'numato 'pyevaṃ pūrū rājye 'bhiṣicyatām /
yaḥ putro guṇasaṃpanno mātāpitrorhitaḥ sadā //
2.68.d:
प्रजा ऊचुः
भवतो ऽनुमतो ऽप्येवं पूरू राज्ये ऽभिषिच्यताम् ।
यः पुत्रो गुणसंपन्नो मातापित्रोर्हितः सदा ॥
2.68.m: The subjects said: / "Since he is approved by you, let Pūru be consecrated in the kingdom. / That son who is endowed with virtues, ever beneficial to mother and father,

2.68.s:
sarvamarhati kalyāṇaṃ kanīyānapi sa prabhuḥ /
arhe 'sya pūrū rājyasya yaḥ priyaḥ priyakṛttava //
2.68.d:
सर्वमर्हति कल्याणं कनीयानपि स प्रभुः ।
अर्हे ऽस्य पूरू राज्यस्य यः प्रियः प्रियकृत्तव ॥
2.68.m: deserves all auspiciousness, even though he is the youngest, O lord. / This Pūru is worthy of the kingdom, who is dear to you and does what is dear to you;

2.68.s:
varadānena śukrasya na śakyaṃ vaktumuttaram /
paurajāna padaistuṣṭairityukte nāhuṣastadā //
2.68.d:
वरदानेन शुक्रस्य न शक्यं वक्तुमुत्तरम् ।
पौरजान पदैस्तुष्टैरित्युक्ते नाहुषस्तदा ॥
2.68.m: because of the granting of a boon by Śukra, it is not possible to speak an objection." / When this was spoken by the contented citizens and countryfolk, Nahuṣa's son then,

2.68.s:
abhiṣicya tataḥ pūruṃ sa rājye sutamātmanaḥ /
diśi dakṣiṇapūrvasyāṃ turvasuṃ tu nyaveśayat //
2.68.d:
अभिषिच्य ततः पूरुं स राज्ये सुतमात्मनः ।
दिशि दक्षिणपूर्वस्यां तुर्वसुं तु न्यवेशयत् ॥
2.68.m: having consecrated his son Pūru in the kingdom, / established Turvasu in the southeast direction.

2.68.s:
dakṣiṇāparato rājā yaduṃ jyeṣṭhaṃ nyaveśayat /
pratīcyāmuttarasyāṃ ca druhyuṃ cānuṃ ca tāvubhau //
2.68.d:
दक्षिणापरतो राजा यदुं ज्येष्ठं न्यवेशयत् ।
प्रतीच्यामुत्तरस्यां च द्रुह्युं चानुं च तावुभौ ॥
2.68.m: The king established his eldest, Yadu, in the southwest, / and Druhyu and Anu, both of them, in the west and north.

2.68.s:
saptadvīpāṃ yayātistu jitvā pṛthvīṃ sasāgarām /
vyabhajatpañcadhā rājā putrebhyo nāhuṣastadā //
2.68.d:
सप्तद्वीपां ययातिस्तु जित्वा पृथ्वीं ससागराम् ।
व्यभजत्पञ्चधा राजा पुत्रेभ्यो नाहुषस्तदा ॥
2.68.m: Having conquered the earth with its seven continents and its oceans, / King Yayāti, son of Nahuṣa, then divided it fivefold among his sons.

2.68.s:
tairiyaṃ pṛthivī sarvā saptadvīpā sapattanā /
yathāpradeśaṃ dharmajñairdharmeṇa pratipānyate //
2.68.d:
तैरियं पृथिवी सर्वा सप्तद्वीपा सपत्तना ।
यथाप्रदेशं धर्मज्ञैर्धर्मेण प्रतिपान्यते ॥
2.68.m: By them this entire earth of seven continents with its cities / is protected righteously according to region by those who know righteousness.

2.68.s:
evaṃ vibhajya pṛthivīṃ putrebhyo nāhuṣastadā /
putrasaṃkrāmitaśrīstu prītimā nabhavannṛpaḥ //
2.68.d:
एवं विभज्य पृथिवीं पुत्रेभ्यो नाहुषस्तदा ।
पुत्रसंक्रामितश्रीस्तु प्रीतिमा नभवन्नृपः ॥
2.68.m: Having thus divided the earth among his sons then, / the king, Nahuṣa's son, having transferred sovereignty to his son, became delighted.

2.68.s:
dhanurnyasya pṛṣatkāṃśca rājyaṃ caiva suteṣu tu /
prītimānabhavadrājā bhāramāveśya bandhuṣu //
2.68.d:
धनुर्न्यस्य पृषत्कांश्च राज्यं चैव सुतेषु तु ।
प्रीतिमानभवद्राजा भारमावेश्य बन्धुषु ॥
2.68.m: Laying down his bow and arrows and the kingdom to his sons, / the king, having placed the burden upon his kin, was joyful.

2.68.s:
atra gāthā mahārājñā purā gītā yayātinā /
yābhiḥ pratyāharetkāmātkūrmauṃ'gānīva sarvaśaḥ //
2.68.d:
अत्र गाथा महाराज्ञा पुरा गीता ययातिना ।
याभिः प्रत्याहरेत्कामात्कूर्मौंऽगानीव सर्वशः ॥
2.68.m: On this matter, verses were sung in ancient times by the great king Yayāti, / by which one should withdraw desires from all sides like a tortoise its limbs:

2.68.s:
na jātu kāmaḥ kāmānamupabhogena śāmyati /
haviṣā kṛṣṇavartmeva bhūya evābhivarddhate //
2.68.d:
न जातु कामः कामानमुपभोगेन शाम्यति ।
हविषा कृष्णवर्त्मेव भूय एवाभिवर्द्धते ॥
2.68.m: "Desire is never pacified by the enjoyment of desires; / it only increases further, like fire with clarified butter.

2.68.s:
yatpṛthivyāṃ vrīhiyavaṃ hiraṇyaṃ paśavaḥ striyaḥ /
nālamekasya tatsarvamiti paśyanna muhyati //
2.68.d:
यत्पृथिव्यां व्रीहियवं हिरण्यं पशवः स्त्रियः ।
नालमेकस्य तत्सर्वमिति पश्यन्न मुह्यति ॥
2.68.m: All the rice, barley, gold, beasts, and women that are on earth / are not enough for one [man]—seeing thus, one is not deluded.

2.68.s:
yadā na kurute bhāvaṃ sarvabhūteṣvamaṅgalam /
karmaṇā manasā vācā brahma saṃpadyate tadā //
2.68.d:
यदा न कुरुते भावं सर्वभूतेष्वमङ्गलम् ।
कर्मणा मनसा वाचा ब्रह्म संपद्यते तदा ॥
2.68.m: When one harbors no ill will toward all beings / in deed, mind, or speech, then one attains Brahman.

2.68.s:
yadā parānna bibheti yadānyasmānna bibhyati /
yadā necchati na dveṣṭi brahma saṃpadyate tadā //
2.68.d:
यदा परान्न बिभेति यदान्यस्मान्न बिभ्यति ।
यदा नेच्छति न द्वेष्टि ब्रह्म संपद्यते तदा ॥
2.68.m: When one does not fear others, and when others do not fear one, / when one neither desires nor hates, then one attains Brahman.

2.68.s:
yā dustyajā durmatibhiryā na jīryati jīryataḥ /
yaiṣā prāṇāntiko rogastāṃ tṛṣṇāṃ tyajataḥ sukham //
2.68.d:
या दुस्त्यजा दुर्मतिभिर्या न जीर्यति जीर्यतः ।
यैषा प्राणान्तिको रोगस्तां तृष्णां त्यजतः सुखम् ॥
2.68.m: That which is hard to abandon by the foolish, which does not age as one ages, / which is a disease that ends only with life—there is happiness for one who abandons that craving.

2.68.s:
jīryanti jīryataḥ keśā dantā jīryanti jīryataḥ /
jīvitāśā dhanāśā ca jīryato 'pi na jīryati //
2.68.d:
जीर्यन्ति जीर्यतः केशा दन्ता जीर्यन्ति जीर्यतः ।
जीविताशा धनाशा च जीर्यतो ऽपि न जीर्यति ॥
2.68.m: Hair turns old as one ages; teeth wear down as one ages; / the hope for life and the hope for wealth do not wear out even as one ages.

2.68.s:
yacca kāmasukhaṃ loke yaccha divyaṃ mahatsukham /
kṛṣṇākṣayasukhasyaitatkalāṃ narhanti ṣoḍaśīm //
2.68.d:
यच्च कामसुखं लोके यच्छ दिव्यं महत्सुखम् ।
कृष्णाक्षयसुखस्यैतत्कलां नर्हन्ति षोडशीम् ॥
2.68.m: Whatever sensual pleasure there is in the world, and whatever great divine pleasure, / these do not equal a sixteenth part of the imperishable happiness of Kṛṣṇa."

2.68.s:
evamuktvā sa rājarṣiḥ sadāraḥ prasthito vanam /
bhṛgutuṅge tapastaptvā tatraiva ca mahāyaśāḥ //
2.68.d:
एवमुक्त्वा स राजर्षिः सदारः प्रस्थितो वनम् ।
भृगुतुङ्गे तपस्तप्त्वा तत्रैव च महायशाः ॥
2.68.m: Having spoken thus, that royal sage set out for the forest with his wife; / and having performed austerities at Bhṛgutuṅga, the highly renowned one there itself,

2.68.s:
pālayitvā vrataṃ cārṣaṃ tatraiva svarga māptavān /
tasya vaṃśāstu pañcaite puṇyā devarṣisatkṛtāḥ //
2.68.d:
पालयित्वा व्रतं चार्षं तत्रैव स्वर्ग माप्तवान् ।
तस्य वंशास्तु पञ्चैते पुण्या देवर्षिसत्कृताः ॥
2.68.m: having kept the vow of the sages, attained heaven right there. / These five holy lineages of his were honored by divine sages,

2.68.s:
yairvyāptā pṛthivī kṛtsnā sūryasyeva gabhastibhiḥ /
dhanyaḥ prajāvā nāyuṣmānkīrttimāṃśca bhavennaraḥ //
2.68.d:
यैर्व्याप्ता पृथिवी कृत्स्ना सूर्यस्येव गभस्तिभिः ।
धन्यः प्रजावा नायुष्मान्कीर्त्तिमांश्च भवेन्नरः ॥
2.68.m: by which the whole earth was pervaded, like [the sky] by the rays of the sun. / A man [who hears this] shall become blessed, possessing offspring, long-lived, and renowned.

2.68.s:
yayāteścāritaṃ sarvaṃ paṭhañchṛṇvandvijottamāḥ //
iti śrībrahmāṇḍe mahāpurāṇe vāyuprokte madhyamabhāge tṛtīya upoddhātapāde aṣṭaṣaṣṭitamo 'dhyāyaḥ // 68//
2.68.d:
ययातेश्चारितं सर्वं पठञ्छृण्वन्द्विजोत्तमाः ॥
इति श्रीब्रह्माण्डे महापुराणे वायुप्रोक्ते मध्यमभागे तृतीय उपोद्धातपादे अष्टषष्टितमो ऽध्यायः ॥ 68॥
2.68.m:
reading or hearing the entire deeds of Yayāti, O best of the twice-born.

Thus ends the sixty-eighth chapter in the Upoddhātapāda, the third section of the Madhyamabhāga, in the venerable Brahmāṇḍa Mahāpurāṇa spoken by Vāyu. // 68

2.69.s:
sūta uvāca
yadorvaṃśaṃ pravakṣyāmi jyeṣṭhasyottamatejasaḥ /
vistareṇānupūrvyā ca gadato me nibodhata //
2.69.d:
सूत उवाच
यदोर्वंशं प्रवक्ष्यामि ज्येष्ठस्योत्तमतेजसः ।
विस्तरेणानुपूर्व्या च गदतो मे निबोधत ॥
2.69.m: The bard said: / I shall proclaim the genealogy of Yadu, the eldest [son] of supreme splendor; / learn it from me as I recount it in detail and in proper order.

2.69.s:
yadoḥ putrā babhūvurhi pañca devasutopamāḥ /
sahasrajidatha śreṣṭhaḥ kroṣṭurnīloñjiko laghuḥ //
2.69.d:
यदोः पुत्रा बभूवुर्हि पञ्च देवसुतोपमाः ।
सहस्रजिदथ श्रेष्ठः क्रोष्टुर्नीलोञ्जिको लघुः ॥
2.69.m: Yadu had five sons, equal to the sons of gods: / Sahasrajit, then the eldest Kroṣṭu, Nīla, Añjika, and the youngest.

2.69.s:
sahasrajitsutaḥ śrīmāñchatajinnāma pārthivaḥ /
śatajittanayāḥ khyātastrayaḥ paramadhārmikāḥ //
2.69.d:
सहस्रजित्सुतः श्रीमाञ्छतजिन्नाम पार्थिवः ।
शतजित्तनयाः ख्यातस्त्रयः परमधार्मिकाः ॥
2.69.m: Sahasrajit’s son was the glorious king named Śatajit. / Śatajit had three famous sons of supreme righteousness:

2.69.s:
haihayaśca hayaschaiva rājā veṇu hayastathā /
haihayasya tu dāyādo dharmanetra iti śrutaḥ //
2.69.d:
हैहयश्च हयस्छैव राजा वेणु हयस्तथा ।
हैहयस्य तु दायादो धर्मनेत्र इति श्रुतः ॥
2.69.m: Haihaya, Haya, and King Veṇuhaya. / Haihaya’s heir was renowned as Dharmanetra.

2.69.s:
dharmanetrasya kuntistu saṃkṣeyastasya cātmajaḥ /
saṃjñeyasya tu dāyādo mahiṣmānnāma pārthivaḥ //
2.69.d:
धर्मनेत्रस्य कुन्तिस्तु संक्षेयस्तस्य चात्मजः ।
संज्ञेयस्य तु दायादो महिष्मान्नाम पार्थिवः ॥
2.69.m: Dharmanetra’s [son] was Kunti, and his son was Saṃkṣeya. / Saṃjñeya’s heir was the king named Mahiṣmat.

2.69.s:
āsīnmahiṣmataḥ putro bhadramenaḥ pratāpavān /
vārāṇasyadhipo rājā kathitaḥ pūrva eva hi //
2.69.d:
आसीन्महिष्मतः पुत्रो भद्रमेनः प्रतापवान् ।
वाराणस्यधिपो राजा कथितः पूर्व एव हि ॥
2.69.m: Mahiṣmat had a son, the majestic Bhadrasena. / He was the king, ruler of Vārāṇasī, mentioned earlier.

2.69.s:
bhadra senasya dāyādo durmado nāma pārthivaḥ /
durmadasyasuto dhīmānkanako nāma viśrutaḥ //
2.69.d:
भद्र सेनस्य दायादो दुर्मदो नाम पार्थिवः ।
दुर्मदस्यसुतो धीमान्कनको नाम विश्रुतः ॥
2.69.m: Bhadrasena’s heir was the king named Durmada. / Durmada’s wise son was renowned as Kanaka.

2.69.s:
kanakasya tu dāyādāścatvāro lokaviśrutāḥ /
kṛtavīryaḥ kṛtāgniśca kṛtavarmā tathaiva ca //
2.69.d:
कनकस्य तु दायादाश्चत्वारो लोकविश्रुताः ।
कृतवीर्यः कृताग्निश्च कृतवर्मा तथैव च ॥
2.69.m: Kanaka had four heirs, world-renowned: / Kṛtavīrya, Kṛtāgni, and likewise Kṛtavarman,

2.69.s:
kṛtaujāśca caturtho 'bhūtkṛtavīryātmajor'junaḥ /
jajñe bāhusahasreṇa saptadvīpeśvaro nṛpaḥ //
2.69.d:
कृतौजाश्च चतुर्थो ऽभूत्कृतवीर्यात्मजोर्ऽजुनः ।
जज्ञे बाहुसहस्रेण सप्तद्वीपेश्वरो नृपः ॥
2.69.m: and Kṛtaujas was the fourth. Kṛtavīrya’s son was Arjuna; / born with a thousand arms, that king became lord of the seven continents.

2.69.s:
sa hi varṣāyutaṃ taptvā tapaḥ paramaduścaram /
dattamārādhayāmāsa kārttavīryo 'trisaṃbhavam //
2.69.d:
स हि वर्षायुतं तप्त्वा तपः परमदुश्चरम् ।
दत्तमाराधयामास कार्त्तवीर्यो ऽत्रिसंभवम् ॥
2.69.m: Having performed supreme, difficult austerities for ten thousand years, / Kārttavīrya propitiated Datta, born of Atri.

2.69.s:
tasmai datto varānprādācca turo bhūritejasaḥ /
pūrvaṃ bāhusahasraṃ tu sa vavre prathamaṃ varam //
2.69.d:
तस्मै दत्तो वरान्प्रादाच्च तुरो भूरितेजसः ।
पूर्वं बाहुसहस्रं तु स वव्रे प्रथमं वरम् ॥
2.69.m: Datta granted him of immense splendor four boons. / First, he chose a thousand arms as the first boon:

2.69.s:
adharmaṃ dhyāyamānasya sahasāsmānnivāraṇam /
dharmeṇa pṛthivīṃ jitvā dharmeṇaivānupālanam //
2.69.d:
अधर्मं ध्यायमानस्य सहसास्मान्निवारणम् ।
धर्मेण पृथिवीं जित्वा धर्मेणैवानुपालनम् ॥
2.69.m: "Sudden restraint from unrighteousness whenever I contemplate unrighteousness; / having conquered the earth by righteousness, protecting it solely through righteousness;

2.69.s:
saṃgrāmāṃstu bahuñjitvā hatvā cārīnsahasraśaḥ /
saṃgrāme yudhyamānasya vadhaḥ syātpradhane mama //
2.69.d:
संग्रामांस्तु बहुञ्जित्वा हत्वा चारीन्सहस्रशः ।
संग्रामे युध्यमानस्य वधः स्यात्प्रधने मम ॥
2.69.m: and having won many battles and slain thousands of foes, / may my death occur in battle, while fighting in combat."

2.69.s:
teneyaṃ pṛthivī kṛtsnā saptadvīpā sapattanā /
saptodadhiparikṣiptā kṣatreṇa vidhinā jitā //
2.69.d:
तेनेयं पृथिवी कृत्स्ना सप्तद्वीपा सपत्तना ।
सप्तोदधिपरिक्षिप्ता क्षत्रेण विधिना जिता ॥
2.69.m: By him, this entire earth with its seven continents and cities, / encircled by the seven oceans, was conquered according to the warrior's rule.

2.69.s:
tasya bāhusahasraṃ tu yudhyataḥ kilayogataḥ /
yogo yogeśvarasyeva prādurbhavati māyayā //
2.69.d:
तस्य बाहुसहस्रं तु युध्यतः किलयोगतः ।
योगो योगेश्वरस्येव प्रादुर्भवति मायया ॥
2.69.m: When he fought, his thousand arms appeared indeed by yoga, / just as the yogic power of a lord of yoga [manifests] through illusion.

2.69.s:
tena saptasu dvīpeṣu saptayajñaśatāni vai /
kṛtāni vidhinā rājñā śrūyate munisattamāḥ //
2.69.d:
तेन सप्तसु द्वीपेषु सप्तयज्ञशतानि वै ।
कृतानि विधिना राज्ञा श्रूयते मुनिसत्तमाः ॥
2.69.m: By that king, across the seven continents, seven hundred sacrifices / were performed according to the rule, so it is heard, O best of sages.

2.69.s:
sarve yajñā mahābāhostasyāmanbhūritejasaḥ /
sarve kāñcanavedīkāḥ sarve yūpaiśca kāñcanaiḥ //
2.69.d:
सर्वे यज्ञा महाबाहोस्तस्यामन्भूरितेजसः ।
सर्वे काञ्चनवेदीकाः सर्वे यूपैश्च काञ्चनैः ॥
2.69.m: All the sacrifices of that long-armed [king] of immense splendor / had golden altars and golden sacrificial posts.

2.69.s:
sarvairdevairmahābhāgai rvimānasthairalaṅkṛtāḥ /
gandharvairapsarobhiśca nityamevopaśobhitāḥ //
2.69.d:
सर्वैर्देवैर्महाभागै र्विमानस्थैरलङ्कृताः ।
गन्धर्वैरप्सरोभिश्च नित्यमेवोपशोभिताः ॥
2.69.m: They were adorned by all the illustrious gods standing in their aerial chariots, / and constantly graced by Gandharvas and Apsarases.

2.69.s:
tasya rājño jagau gāthāṃ gandharvo nāradastadā /
caritaṃ tasya rājarṣermahimānaṃ nirīkṣya ca //
2.69.d:
तस्य राज्ञो जगौ गाथां गन्धर्वो नारदस्तदा ।
चरितं तस्य राजर्षेर्महिमानं निरीक्ष्य च ॥
2.69.m: Then the Gandharva Nārada sang a song about that king, / seeing the deeds and the greatness of that royal sage:

2.69.s:
na nūnaṃ kārttavīryasya gatiṃ yāsyanti mānavāḥ /
yajñairdānaistapobhiśca vikrameṇa śrutena ca //
2.69.d:
न नूनं कार्त्तवीर्यस्य गतिं यास्यन्ति मानवाः ।
यज्ञैर्दानैस्तपोभिश्च विक्रमेण श्रुतेन च ॥
2.69.m: "Surely no mortal men will attain the state of Kārttavīrya / through sacrifices, gifts, austerities, valor, or sacred knowledge."

2.69.s:
dvīpeṣu saptasu sa vai dhanvī khaḍgī śārāsanī /
rathī rājā sānucaro yogāccaivānudṛśyate //
2.69.d:
द्वीपेषु सप्तसु स वै धन्वी खड्गी शारासनी ।
रथी राजा सानुचरो योगाच्चैवानुदृश्यते ॥
2.69.m: Across the seven continents, that king—bearing a bow, sword, and arrows, / riding a chariot with his attendants—was perceived through yoga.

2.69.s:
anaṣṭadravyatā cāsīnna kleśo na ca vibhramaḥ /
prabhāveṇa mahārājñaḥ prajā dharmeṇa rakṣitaḥ //
2.69.d:
अनष्टद्रव्यता चासीन्न क्लेशो न च विभ्रमः ।
प्रभावेण महाराज्ञः प्रजा धर्मेण रक्षितः ॥
2.69.m: No property was lost, there was neither distress nor confusion; / through the majesty of the great king, the subjects were protected with righteousness.

2.69.s:
pañcāśītisahasrāṇi varṣāṇāṃ sa narādhipaḥ /
sa sarvaratnabhāksa mrāṭ cakravartī babhūva ha //
2.69.d:
पञ्चाशीतिसहस्राणि वर्षाणां स नराधिपः ।
स सर्वरत्नभाक्स म्राट् चक्रवर्ती बभूव ह ॥
2.69.m: For eighty-five thousand years, that ruler of men / was an emperor possessing all treasures, a universal monarch.

2.69.s:
sa eṣa paśupālo 'bhūtkṣetrapālastathai va ca /
sa eva vṛṣṭyā parjanyo yogitvādarjuno 'bhavat //
2.69.d:
स एष पशुपालो ऽभूत्क्षेत्रपालस्तथै व च ।
स एव वृष्ट्या पर्जन्यो योगित्वादर्जुनो ऽभवत् ॥
2.69.m: He was the protector of cattle and also the guardian of the fields; / through his yoga, Arjuna himself became Parjanya [providing rain] through his showers.

2.69.s:
sa ve bāhusahasreṇa jyāghātakaṭhinena ca /
bhāti raśmisahasreṇa śāradenaiva bhāskaraḥ //
2.69.d:
स वे बाहुसहस्रेण ज्याघातकठिनेन च ।
भाति रश्मिसहस्रेण शारदेनैव भास्करः ॥
2.69.m: With his thousand arms hardened by the strike of the bowstring, / he shone like the sun with its thousand rays in autumn.

2.69.s:
sa hi nāgasahakreṇa māhiṣmatyāṃ narādhipaḥ /
karkoṭakasabhāṃ jitvā purīṃ tatra nyaveśayat //
2.69.d:
स हि नागसहक्रेण माहिष्मत्यां नराधिपः ।
कर्कोटकसभां जित्वा पुरीं तत्र न्यवेशयत् ॥
2.69.m: With a thousand elephants, that king / conquered the assembly of Karkoṭaka at Māhiṣmatī and founded his city there.

2.69.s:
sa vai vegaṃ samudrasya prāvṛṭkāleṃbujekṣaṇaḥ /
krīḍanneva sukhodvignaḥ prāvṛṭkālaṃ cakāra ha //
2.69.d:
स वै वेगं समुद्रस्य प्रावृट्कालेंबुजेक्षणः ।
क्रीडन्नेव सुखोद्विग्नः प्रावृट्कालं चकार ह ॥
2.69.m: The lotus-eyed [king], while merely playing in the rainy season, / playfully held back the ocean’s surge and caused the rainy season to stir.

2.69.s:
lulitā krīḍatā tena hemasragdāmamālinī /
ūrmimuktārttasannādā śaṅkitābhyeti narmadā //
2.69.d:
लुलिता क्रीडता तेन हेमस्रग्दाममालिनी ।
ऊर्मिमुक्तार्त्तसन्नादा शङ्किताभ्येति नर्मदा ॥
2.69.m: Agitated by him as he played, garlanded with chains of golden wreaths, / the Narmadā flowed anxiously, its cries piteous amidst loosened waves.

2.69.s:
purā bhuja sahasreṇa sa jagāhe mahārmavam /
cakārodvṛttavelaṃ tamakāle mārutoddhatam //
2.69.d:
पुरा भुज सहस्रेण स जगाहे महार्मवम् ।
चकारोद्वृत्तवेलं तमकाले मारुतोद्धतम् ॥
2.69.m: Formerly, with a thousand arms he plunged into the vast ocean, / causing its shoreline to overflow and stirring it up out of season like a tempest.

2.69.s:
tasya bāhusahasreṇa kṣobhyamāṇe mahodadhau /
bhavanti līnā niśceṣṭāḥ pātālasthā mahāsurāḥ //
2.69.d:
तस्य बाहुसहस्रेण क्षोभ्यमाणे महोदधौ ।
भवन्ति लीना निश्चेष्टाः पातालस्था महासुराः ॥
2.69.m: When the great ocean was churned by his thousand arms, / the great asuras dwelling in Pātāla lay concealed and motionless.

2.69.s:
cūrṇīkṛtamahāvīcilīnamīnamahāviṣam /
patitāviddhaphenaughamāvarttakṣiptadussaham //
2.69.d:
चूर्णीकृतमहावीचिलीनमीनमहाविषम् ।
पतिताविद्धफेनौघमावर्त्तक्षिप्तदुस्सहम् ॥
2.69.m: Its great waves crushed to powder, its great poisonous fish lying concealed, / its masses of foam cast down and scattered, unbearable when tossed into whirlpools,

2.69.s:
cakāra kṣobhayanrājā doḥsahasreṇa sāgaram /
devāsuraparikṣiptaṃ kṣīrodamiva sāgaram //
2.69.d:
चकार क्षोभयन्राजा दोःसहस्रेण सागरम् ।
देवासुरपरिक्षिप्तं क्षीरोदमिव सागरम् ॥
2.69.m: churning the ocean with his thousand arms, the king made it resemble / the ocean of milk churned by gods and asuras,

2.69.s:
mandarakṣobhaṇabhrāntamamṛtotpatti hetave /
sahasā vidrutā bhītā bhīmaṃ dṛṣṭvā nṛpottamam //
2.69.d:
मन्दरक्षोभणभ्रान्तममृतोत्पत्ति हेतवे ।
सहसा विद्रुता भीता भीमं दृष्ट्वा नृपोत्तमम् ॥
2.69.m: whirled by the churning of Mandara for the sake of the production of nectar. / Frightened on seeing the dreadful best of kings, they fled at once,

2.69.s:
niścitaṃ natamūrddhāno babhūvuśca mahoragāḥ /
sāyāhne kadalīkhañca nivātestamitā iva //
2.69.d:
निश्चितं नतमूर्द्धानो बभूवुश्च महोरगाः ।
सायाह्ने कदलीखञ्च निवातेस्तमिता इव ॥
2.69.m: and the great serpents bowed their heads firmly, / like a clump of plantain trees standing motionless in the evening windlessness.

2.69.s:
jyāmāropya dṛḍhe cāpe sāyakaiḥ pañcabhiḥ śataiḥ /
laṅkeśaṃ mohayitvā tu sabalaṃ rāvaṇaṃ balāt //
2.69.d:
ज्यामारोप्य दृढे चापे सायकैः पञ्चभिः शतैः ।
लङ्केशं मोहयित्वा तु सबलं रावणं बलात् ॥
2.69.m: Fitting a string onto his sturdy bow, with five hundred arrows / he bewildered Rāvaṇa, the lord of Laṅkā, along with his army by force;

2.69.s:
nirjitya vaśamānīya māhiṣmatyāṃ babandha tam /
tato gatvā pulastyastamarjunaṃ ca prasādhayat //
2.69.d:
निर्जित्य वशमानीय माहिष्मत्यां बबन्ध तम् ।
ततो गत्वा पुलस्त्यस्तमर्जुनं च प्रसाधयत् ॥
2.69.m: having subdued him and brought him under his control, he bound him in Māhiṣmatī. / Thereupon Pulastya went and appeased Arjuna.

2.69.s:
mumoca rājā paulastyaṃ pulastyenā nuyācitaḥ /
tasya bāhusahasrasya babhūva jyātalasvanaḥ //
2.69.d:
मुमोच राजा पौलस्त्यं पुलस्त्येना नुयाचितः ।
तस्य बाहुसहस्रस्य बभूव ज्यातलस्वनः ॥
2.69.m: Entreated by Pulastya, the king released the son of Pulastya. / The sound of the bowstrings on his thousand arms was

2.69.s:
yugānteṃbudavṛndasya sphuṭitasyāśaneriva /
aho mṛdhe mahāvīryo bhārgavastasya yo 'cchinat //
2.69.d:
युगान्तेंबुदवृन्दस्य स्फुटितस्याशनेरिव ।
अहो मृधे महावीर्यो भार्गवस्तस्य यो ऽच्छिनत् ॥
2.69.m: like the crash of a mass of clouds bursting with lightning at the end of an age. / Oh, how exceedingly valiant was the Bhārgava who, in combat, severed

2.69.s:
mṛdhe sahasraṃ bāhunāṃ hematālavanaṃ yathā /
tṛṣitena kadācitsa bhikṣitaścitrabhānunā //
2.69.d:
मृधे सहस्रं बाहुनां हेमतालवनं यथा ।
तृषितेन कदाचित्स भिक्षितश्चित्रभानुना ॥
2.69.m: that thousand of arms in battle, as if a forest of golden palm trees! / Once, being hungry, the Fire-god begged him for alms;

2.69.s:
saptadvīpāṃścitrabhānoḥ prādadbhikṣāṃ viśāṃpatiḥ /
purāṇi ghoṣāngrāmāṃśca pattanāni ca sarvaśaḥ //
2.69.d:
सप्तद्वीपांश्चित्रभानोः प्रादद्भिक्षां विशांपतिः ।
पुराणि घोषान्ग्रामांश्च पत्तनानि च सर्वशः ॥
2.69.m: the lord of the subjects gave the seven continents to the Fire-god as alms, / the cities, cowherd stations, villages, and ports everywhere.

2.69.s:
jajvāla tasya bāṇeṣu citrābhānurdidhakṣayā /
sa tasya puruṣendrasya pratāpena mahāyaśāḥ //
2.69.d:
जज्वाल तस्य बाणेषु चित्राभानुर्दिधक्षया ।
स तस्य पुरुषेन्द्रस्य प्रतापेन महायशाः ॥
2.69.m: Desiring to burn, the Fire-god blazed among his arrows; / through the majesty of that best of men, that highly renowned one

2.69.s:
dadāha kārttavīryasya śailāṃścāpi vanāni ca /
sa śūnyamāśramaṃ sarvaṃ varuṇasyātmajasya vai //
2.69.d:
ददाह कार्त्तवीर्यस्य शैलांश्चापि वनानि च ।
स शून्यमाश्रमं सर्वं वरुणस्यात्मजस्य वै ॥
2.69.m: burned the mountains and forests of Kārttavīrya. / Then that Haihaya and the Fire-god burned the entire deserted hermitage

2.69.s:
dadāha savanāṭopaṃ citrabhānuḥ sa haihayaḥ /
yaṃ lebhe varuṇaḥ putraṃ purā bhāsvantamuttamam //
2.69.d:
ददाह सवनाटोपं चित्रभानुः स हैहयः ।
यं लेभे वरुणः पुत्रं पुरा भास्वन्तमुत्तमम् ॥
2.69.m: of the son of Varuṇa, along with its dense woods. / The radiant, supreme son whom Varuṇa formerly obtained,

2.69.s:
vasiṣṭhanāmā sa muniḥ khyāta āpava ityuta /
tatrāpavastadā krodhādarjunaṃ śaptavānvibhuḥ //
2.69.d:
वसिष्ठनामा स मुनिः ख्यात आपव इत्युत ।
तत्रापवस्तदा क्रोधादर्जुनं शप्तवान्विभुः ॥
2.69.m: that sage named Vasiṣṭha was also known as Āpava. / Thereupon the powerful Āpava cursed Arjuna in wrath:

2.69.s:
yasmānnavarjitamidaṃ vanaṃ te mama haihaya /
tasmātte duṣkaraṃ karma kṛtamanyo haniṣyati //
2.69.d:
यस्मान्नवर्जितमिदं वनं ते मम हैहय ।
तस्मात्ते दुष्करं कर्म कृतमन्यो हनिष्यति ॥
2.69.m: "Because this forest of mine was not spared by you, O Haihaya, / therefore another will undo the difficult deed accomplished by you.

2.69.s:
arjuno nāma kainteyaḥ sa ca rājā bhaviṣyati /
arjunaṃ ca mahāvīryo rāmaḥ praharatāṃ varaḥ //
2.69.d:
अर्जुनो नाम कैन्तेयः स च राजा भविष्यति ।
अर्जुनं च महावीर्यो रामः प्रहरतां वरः ॥
2.69.m: There shall be an Arjuna, the son of Kuntī, who will be a king; / and as for [this] Arjuna, the mighty Rāma, best among strikers,

2.69.s:
chittvā bāhusahasraṃ vai pramathya tarasā balī /
tapasvī brāhmaṇaścaiva vadhiṣyati mahābalaḥ //
2.69.d:
छित्त्वा बाहुसहस्रं वै प्रमथ्य तरसा बली ।
तपस्वी ब्राह्मणश्चैव वधिष्यति महाबलः ॥
2.69.m: having severed his thousand arms and crushed him swiftly by force, / that mighty ascetic and brāhmaṇa of great strength will slay [him]."

2.69.s:
tasya rāmastadā hyāsīnmṛtyuḥ śāpena dhīmataḥ /
rājñā tena varaścaiva svayameva vṛtaḥ purā //
2.69.d:
तस्य रामस्तदा ह्यासीन्मृत्युः शापेन धीमतः ।
राज्ञा तेन वरश्चैव स्वयमेव वृतः पुरा ॥
2.69.m: Rāma then became his death through the curse of that wise [sage]; / and formerly that king himself had chosen that boon.

2.69.s:
tasya putraśataṃ tvāsītpañca tatra mahārathāḥ /
kṛtāstrā balinaḥ śūrā dharmātmāno yaśasvinaḥ //
2.69.d:
तस्य पुत्रशतं त्वासीत्पञ्च तत्र महारथाः ।
कृतास्त्रा बलिनः शूरा धर्मात्मानो यशस्विनः ॥
2.69.m: He had a hundred sons, of whom five were great chariot-warriors, / trained in weapons, mighty, heroic, righteous, and renowned:

2.69.s:
śūraśca śūrasenaśca vṛṣāsyo vṛṣa eva ca /
jayadhvajo vaṃśakarttā avantiṣu viśāṃpatiḥ //
2.69.d:
शूरश्च शूरसेनश्च वृषास्यो वृष एव च ।
जयध्वजो वंशकर्त्ता अवन्तिषु विशांपतिः ॥
2.69.m: Śūra, Śūrasena, Vṛṣāsya, Vṛṣa, / and Jayadhvaja, the founder of the dynasty, lord of subjects among the Avantis.

2.69.s:
jayadhvajasya putrastu tālajaṅghaḥ pratāpavān /
tasya putraśataṃ tvevaṃ tālajaṅghā itiśrutam //
2.69.d:
जयध्वजस्य पुत्रस्तु तालजङ्घः प्रतापवान् ।
तस्य पुत्रशतं त्वेवं तालजङ्घा इतिश्रुतम् ॥
2.69.m: Jayadhvaja’s son was the powerful Tālajaṅgha; / his hundred sons are thus known as the Tālajaṅghas.

2.69.s:
teṣāṃ pañca gaṇāḥ khyātā haihayānāṃ mahātmanām /
vītihotrāśca saṃjātā bhojāścāvantayastathā //
2.69.d:
तेषां पञ्च गणाः ख्याता हैहयानां महात्मनाम् ।
वीतिहोत्राश्च संजाता भोजाश्चावन्तयस्तथा ॥
2.69.m: Five groups of those high-souled Haihayas are renowned: / the Vītihotras were born, and the Bhojas, and likewise the Āvantyas,

2.69.s:
tuṇḍikerāśca vikrāntāstālajaṅghāstathaiva ca /
vītihotrasutaścāpi ananto nāma pārthivaḥ //
2.69.d:
तुण्डिकेराश्च विक्रान्तास्तालजङ्घास्तथैव च ।
वीतिहोत्रसुतश्चापि अनन्तो नाम पार्थिवः ॥
2.69.m: the valiant Tuṇḍikeras, and likewise the Tālajaṅghas. / And the son of Vītihotra was the king named Ananta.

2.69.s:
durjayastasya putrastu babhūvāmitrakarśanaḥ /
anaṣṭa dravyatā caiva tasya rājño babhūva ha //
2.69.d:
दुर्जयस्तस्य पुत्रस्तु बभूवामित्रकर्शनः ।
अनष्ट द्रव्यता चैव तस्य राज्ञो बभूव ह ॥
2.69.m: His son was Durjaya, the crusher of enemies. / Indeed, that king never suffered loss of property;

2.69.s:
prabhāveṇa mahārājaḥ prajāstāḥ paryapālayat /
na tasya vittanāśaḥ syānnaṣṭaṃ pratilabhecca saḥ //
2.69.d:
प्रभावेण महाराजः प्रजास्ताः पर्यपालयत् ।
न तस्य वित्तनाशः स्यान्नष्टं प्रतिलभेच्च सः ॥
2.69.m: by his prowess the great king protected those subjects. / He suffered no loss of wealth, and whatever was lost he would recover.

2.69.s:
kārttavīryasya yo janma kathayediha dhīmataḥ /
varddhante vibhavāśśaśvaddharmaścāsya vivarddhate //
2.69.d:
कार्त्तवीर्यस्य यो जन्म कथयेदिह धीमतः ।
वर्द्धन्ते विभवाश्शश्वद्धर्मश्चास्य विवर्द्धते ॥
2.69.m: Whoever narrates here the birth of the wise Kārttavīrya, / his possessions ever increase and his righteousness grows.

2.69.s:
yathā yaṣṭā yathā dātā tathā svarge mahīpate //
iti śrībrahmāṇḍe mahopurāṇe vāyuprokte madhyamabhāge tṛtīya upoddhātapāde bhārgavacarite kārttavīryasaṃbhavo nāma ekonasaptatitamo 'dhyāyaḥ
2.69.d:
यथा यष्टा यथा दाता तथा स्वर्गे महीपते ॥
इति श्रीब्रह्माण्डे महोपुराणे वायुप्रोक्ते मध्यमभागे तृतीय उपोद्धातपादे भार्गवचरिते कार्त्तवीर्यसंभवो नाम एकोनसप्ततितमो ऽध्यायः
2.69.m:
As a sacrificer, as a giver [he lives], so [he rejoices] in heaven, O king.

Thus ends the sixty-ninth chapter, entitled "The Origin of Kārttavīrya", in the story of the Bhārgava in the third Upoddhātapāda of the middle section of the glorious and great Brahmāṇḍapurāṇa proclaimed by Vāyu.

2.70.s:
ṛṣaya ūcuḥ
kimarthaṃ tu vanaṃ dagdhamāpavasya mahātmanaḥ /
kārttavīryeṇa vikramya tannaḥ prabrūhi pṛcchatām //
2.70.d:
ऋषय ऊचुः
किमर्थं तु वनं दग्धमापवस्य महात्मनः ।
कार्त्तवीर्येण विक्रम्य तन्नः प्रब्रूहि पृच्छताम् ॥
2.70.m: The sages said: / For what reason was the forest of the high-souled Āpava burned / by Kārttavīrya having advanced in valor? Tell us who ask this.

2.70.s:
rakṣitā satu rājarṣiḥ prajānāmiti naḥ śrutam /
kathaṃ sarakṣitā bhūtvā nāśayeta tapovanam //
[verses 2,70.3 - 49 not available at present]
2.70.d:
रक्षिता सतु राजर्षिः प्रजानामिति नः श्रुतम् ।
कथं सरक्षिता भूत्वा नाशयेत तपोवनम् ॥
[वेर्सेस् 2,70.3 - 49 नोत् अवैलब्ले अत् प्रेसेन्त्]
2.70.m: We have heard that that royal sage was the protector of his subjects; / having been a protector, how could he destroy a hermitage?

2.71.s:
sūta uvāca
sāttvatājjajñire putrāḥ kauśalyāyāṃ mahābalāḥ /
bhajamāno bhajirddivyo vṛṣṇirdevāvṛdho 'ndhakaḥ //
2.71.d:
सूत उवाच
सात्त्वताज्जज्ञिरे पुत्राः कौशल्यायां महाबलाः ।
भजमानो भजिर्द्दिव्यो वृष्णिर्देवावृधो ऽन्धकः ॥
2.71.m: The bard said: / Mighty sons were born to Sāttvata by Kauśalyā: / Bhajamāna, the divine Bhaji, Vṛṣṇi, Devāvṛdha, Andhaka,

2.71.s:
mahābhojaśca vikhyāto brahmaṇyassatyasaṃgaraḥ /
teṣāṃ hi sargāścatvāraḥ śṛṇudhvaṃ vistareṇa vai //
2.71.d:
महाभोजश्च विख्यातो ब्रह्मण्यस्सत्यसंगरः ।
तेषां हि सर्गाश्चत्वारः शृणुध्वं विस्तरेण वै ॥
2.71.m: and the renowned Mahābhoja, devoted to Brahman, true to his word. / Hear in detail about their four branches of lineage.

2.71.s:
bhajamānasya sṛṃjayyo bāhyakā copavāhyakā /
sṛṃja yasya sute dve tu bāhyake te udāvahat //
2.71.d:
भजमानस्य सृंजय्यो बाह्यका चोपवाह्यका ।
सृंज यस्य सुते द्वे तु बाह्यके ते उदावहत् ॥
2.71.m: Bhajamāna had [two wives] of the Sṛñjaya clan, Bāhyakā and Upavāhyakā; / he married those two daughters of Sṛñjaya, the Bāhyakās.

2.71.s:
tasya bhārye bhaginyau te prasūte tu sutānbahūn /
nimlociḥ kiṅkaṇaścaiva dhṛṣṭiḥ para purañjayaḥ //
2.71.d:
तस्य भार्ये भगिन्यौ ते प्रसूते तु सुतान्बहून् ।
निम्लोचिः किङ्कणश्चैव धृष्टिः पर पुरञ्जयः ॥
2.71.m: His two wives, those sisters, bore many sons: / Nimloci, Kiṅkaṇa, and Dhṛṣṭi, conqueror of enemy cities.

2.71.s:
te bāhyakāyā sṛṃjayyā bhajamānādvijajñire /
ayutājitsahasrājicchatājiditi nāmataḥ //
2.71.d:
ते बाह्यकाया सृंजय्या भजमानाद्विजज्ञिरे ।
अयुताजित्सहस्राजिच्छताजिदिति नामतः ॥
2.71.m: They were born to Bhajamāna from Bāhyakā, daughter of Sṛñjaya; / [and three others] named Ayutājit, Sahasrājit, and Śatājit,

2.71.s:
bāhyakāyāṃ bhaginyāṃ te bhajamānādvijajñire /
teṣāṃ devāvṛdho rājā cacāra paramaṃ tapaḥ /
putraḥ sarvaguṇopeto mama bhūyāditi sma ha //
2.71.d:
बाह्यकायां भगिन्यां ते भजमानाद्विजज्ञिरे ।
तेषां देवावृधो राजा चचार परमं तपः ।
पुत्रः सर्वगुणोपेतो मम भूयादिति स्म ह ॥
2.71.m: they were born to Bhajamāna from the sister Bāhyakā. / Among them, King Devāvṛdha performed supreme austerities, / thinking: "May a son endowed with all good qualities be mine!"

2.71.s: saṃyojyā tmānamevaṃ sa parṇāśajalamaspṛśat //
2.71.d: संयोज्या त्मानमेवं स पर्णाशजलमस्पृशत् ॥
2.71.m: Concentrating himself in this way, he touched the waters of the Parṇāśā.

2.71.s:
sā copasparśanāttasya cakāra priyamāpagā /
kalyāṇatvānnarapatestasya sā nimnagottamā //
2.71.d:
सा चोपस्पर्शनात्तस्य चकार प्रियमापगा ।
कल्याणत्वान्नरपतेस्तस्य सा निम्नगोत्तमा ॥
2.71.m: And that river, by his touching her, acted favorably toward him; / because of that king’s virtue, that best of streams,

2.71.s:
cintayābhiparītāṅgī jagāmātha viniścayam /
nābhigacchāmi tāṃ nārīṃ yasyāmevaṃvidhaḥ sutaḥ //
2.71.d:
चिन्तयाभिपरीताङ्गी जगामाथ विनिश्चयम् ।
नाभिगच्छामि तां नारीं यस्यामेवंविधः सुतः ॥
2.71.m: her body overcome with reflection, came to a decision: / "I see no woman in whom such a son,

2.71.s:
bhavetsarvaguṇopeto rājño devāvṛdhasya hi /
tasmādasya svayaṃ cāhaṃ bhavāmyadya sahavratā //
2.71.d:
भवेत्सर्वगुणोपेतो राज्ञो देवावृधस्य हि ।
तस्मादस्य स्वयं चाहं भवाम्यद्य सहव्रता ॥
2.71.m: endowed with all good qualities, could be born to King Devāvṛdha. / Therefore, I myself shall become his consort today."

2.71.s:
jajñe tasyāḥ svayaṃ hṛtstho bhāvastasya yatheritaḥ /
atha bhūtvā kumārī tu sā cintāparameva ca //
2.71.d:
जज्ञे तस्याः स्वयं हृत्स्थो भावस्तस्य यथेरितः ।
अथ भूत्वा कुमारी तु सा चिन्तापरमेव च ॥
2.71.m: His thought residing in her heart was recognized by her just as it was expressed. / Then, having become a maiden absorbed in contemplation,

2.71.s:
varayāmāsa rājānaṃ tāmiyeṣa sa pārthivaḥ /
tasyāmādhatta garbhe sa tejasvinamudā radhīḥ //
2.71.d:
वरयामास राजानं तामियेष स पार्थिवः ।
तस्यामाधत्त गर्भे स तेजस्विनमुदा रधीः ॥
2.71.m: she chose the king, and that ruler of the earth desired her. / In her womb that noble-minded king deposited a radiant [embryo].

2.71.s:
atha sā navame māsi suṣuve saritā varā /
putraṃ sarvaguṇopetaṃ babhruṃ devāvṛdhattadā //
2.71.d:
अथ सा नवमे मासि सुषुवे सरिता वरा ।
पुत्रं सर्वगुणोपेतं बभ्रुं देवावृधत्तदा ॥
2.71.m: Then, in the ninth month, that best of rivers bore / to Devāvṛdha a son endowed with all virtues, Babhru.

2.71.s:
tatra vaṃśe purāṇajñā gāthāṃ gāyanti vai dvijāḥ /
guṇāndevāvṛdhasyāpi kīrtayanto mahātmanaḥ //
2.71.d:
तत्र वंशे पुराणज्ञा गाथां गायन्ति वै द्विजाः ।
गुणान्देवावृधस्यापि कीर्तयन्तो महात्मनः ॥
2.71.m: In that lineage, twice-born men knowing the Purāṇas sing a song, / also praising the virtues of the high-souled Devāvṛdha:

2.71.s:
yathaiva śṛṇumo dūrātsapaṃśyāmastathāntikāt /
babhruḥ śreṣṭho manuṣyāṇāṃ devairdevāvṛthaḥ samaḥ //
2.71.d:
यथैव शृणुमो दूरात्सपंश्यामस्तथान्तिकात् ।
बभ्रुः श्रेष्ठो मनुष्याणां देवैर्देवावृथः समः ॥
2.71.m: "Just as we hear from afar, so we see near at hand: / Babhru is the foremost of men; Devāvṛdha is equal to the gods.

2.71.s:
puruṣāḥ pañcaṣaṣṭiśca sahasrāṇi ca saptatiḥ /
yemṛtatvamanuprāptā babrordevāvṛdhādapi //
2.71.d:
पुरुषाः पञ्चषष्टिश्च सहस्राणि च सप्ततिः ।
येमृतत्वमनुप्राप्ता बब्रोर्देवावृधादपि ॥
2.71.m: There were sixty-five and seventy thousand men / who attained immortality through Babhru and Devāvṛdha."

2.71.s:
yajvā dānapatirdhīro brahmaṇyaḥ satyavāgbudhaḥ /
kīrttimāṃśca mahābhojaḥ sāttvatānāṃ mahārathaḥ //
2.71.d:
यज्वा दानपतिर्धीरो ब्रह्मण्यः सत्यवाग्बुधः ।
कीर्त्तिमांश्च महाभोजः सात्त्वतानां महारथः ॥
2.71.m: [Babhru was] a sacrificer, lord of gifts, resolute, devoted to Brahman, speaking truth, wise, / renowned, a great Bhoja, and a great chariot-warrior of the Sāttvatas.

2.71.s:
tasyānvavāyaḥ sumahānbhojā ye bhuvi viśrutāḥ /
gāndhārī caiva mādrī ca dhṛṣṭairbhārye babhūvatuḥ //
2.71.d:
तस्यान्ववायः सुमहान्भोजा ये भुवि विश्रुताः ।
गान्धारी चैव माद्री च धृष्टैर्भार्ये बभूवतुः ॥
2.71.m: His lineage is exceedingly great, the Bhojas who are renowned on earth. / Gāndhārī and Mādrī were the two wives of Dhṛṣṭa;

2.71.s:
gāndhārī janayāmāsa sumitraṃ mitranandanam /
sādrī yudhājitaṃ putraṃ tato mīḍhvāṃsameva ca //
2.71.d:
गान्धारी जनयामास सुमित्रं मित्रनन्दनम् ।
साद्री युधाजितं पुत्रं ततो मीढ्वांसमेव च ॥
2.71.m: Gāndhārī gave birth to Sumitra, the delighter of his friends; / Mādrī bore the son Yudhājit, and then Mīḍhvāṃs,

2.71.s:
anamitraṃ śinaṃ caiva tābubhau puruṣottamau /
anamitrasuto nighno nighnasya dvau babhūvatuḥ //
2.71.d:
अनमित्रं शिनं चैव ताबुभौ पुरुषोत्तमौ ।
अनमित्रसुतो निघ्नो निघ्नस्य द्वौ बभूवतुः ॥
2.71.m: Anamitra, and Śina, both of them best among men. / Anamitra’s son was Nighna; Nighna had two sons:

2.71.s:
prasenaśca mahābhāgaḥ satrājicca sutābubhau /
tasya satrājitaḥ sūryaḥ sakhā prāṇasamo 'bhavat //
2.71.d:
प्रसेनश्च महाभागः सत्राजिच्च सुताबुभौ ।
तस्य सत्राजितः सूर्यः सखा प्राणसमो ऽभवत् ॥
2.71.m: the illustrious Prasena and Satrājit were both his sons. / Sūrya became Satrājit’s friend, dear as his own life.

2.71.s:
sa kadācinniśāpāye rathena rathināṃ varaḥ /
toyaṃ kūlātsamuddhartumupasthātuṃ yayauravim //
2.71.d:
स कदाचिन्निशापाये रथेन रथिनां वरः ।
तोयं कूलात्समुद्धर्तुमुपस्थातुं ययौरविम् ॥
2.71.m: Once at the end of night, that best of chariot-warriors / went by chariot to draw water from the bank and worship the Sun.

2.71.s:
tasyopatiṣṭhataḥ sūryaṃ vivasvānagrataḥ sthitaḥ /
suspaṣṭamūrttirbhagavāṃstejomaṇḍalavānvibhuḥ //
2.71.d:
तस्योपतिष्ठतः सूर्यं विवस्वानग्रतः स्थितः ।
सुस्पष्टमूर्त्तिर्भगवांस्तेजोमण्डलवान्विभुः ॥
2.71.m: As he was worshipping the Sun, Vivasvat stood before him, / the lord of very distinct form, possessing a circle of radiance.

2.71.s:
atha rājā vivasvantamuvāca sthitamagrataḥ /
yathaiva vyomni paśyāmi tvāmahaṃ jyotiṣāṃ pate //
2.71.d:
अथ राजा विवस्वन्तमुवाच स्थितमग्रतः ।
यथैव व्योम्नि पश्यामि त्वामहं ज्योतिषां पते ॥
2.71.m: Then the king spoke to Vivasvat who was standing before him: / "Just as I see you in the sky, O lord of heavenly lights,

2.71.s:
tejomaṇḍalinaṃ caiva tathaivāpyagrataḥ sthitam /
ko viśeṣo vivasvaṃste sakhyenopagatasya vai //
2.71.d:
तेजोमण्डलिनं चैव तथैवाप्यग्रतः स्थितम् ।
को विशेषो विवस्वंस्ते सख्येनोपगतस्य वै ॥
2.71.m: possessing a circle of radiance, exactly so [I see you] standing before me. / What distinction is there in you, O Vivasvat, who have approached in friendship?"

2.71.s:
etacchrutvā sa bhagavānmaṇiratnaṃ syamantakam /
svakaṇṭhādavamucyātha babandha nṛpatestadā //
2.71.d:
एतच्छ्रुत्वा स भगवान्मणिरत्नं स्यमन्तकम् ।
स्वकण्ठादवमुच्याथ बबन्ध नृपतेस्तदा ॥
2.71.m: Having heard this, the blessed one then took off the jewel-gem, the Syamantaka, / from his own neck and fastened it on the king.

2.71.s:
tato vigrahavantaṃ taṃ dadarśa nṛpatistadā /
prītimānatha taṃ dṛṣṭvā muhūrttaṃ kṛtavānkathām //
2.71.d:
ततो विग्रहवन्तं तं ददर्श नृपतिस्तदा ।
प्रीतिमानथ तं दृष्ट्वा मुहूर्त्तं कृतवान्कथाम् ॥
2.71.m: Then the king saw him in embodied form; / and seeing him, delighted, he conversed with him for a moment.

2.71.s:
tamabhiprasthitaṃ bhūyo vivasvantaṃ sa satrajit /
provācāgnisavarṇaṃ tvāṃ yena lokaḥ prapaśyati //
2.71.d:
तमभिप्रस्थितं भूयो विवस्वन्तं स सत्रजित् ।
प्रोवाचाग्निसवर्णं त्वां येन लोकः प्रपश्यति ॥
2.71.m: As Vivasvat was departing again, Satrājit / said to him: "By which the world sees you as having the color of fire,

2.71.s:
tadetanmaṇiratnaṃ me bhagavandātumarhasi /
syamaṃ takaṃ nāmamaṇiṃ dattavāṃstasya bhāskaraḥ //
2.71.d:
तदेतन्मणिरत्नं मे भगवन्दातुमर्हसि ।
स्यमं तकं नाममणिं दत्तवांस्तस्य भास्करः ॥
2.71.m: that jewel-gem, O blessed one, you should give to me." / The sun gave him the gem named Syamantaka.

2.71.s:
sa tamāmucya nagarīṃ praviveśa mahīpatiḥ /
vismāpayitvātha tataḥ purīmantaḥpuraṃ yayau //
2.71.d:
स तमामुच्य नगरीं प्रविवेश महीपतिः ।
विस्मापयित्वाथ ततः पुरीमन्तःपुरं ययौ ॥
2.71.m: Having fastened it on, the king entered the city; / having astonished the city, he then went to the inner apartments.

2.71.s:
sa prasenāya taddivyaṃ maṇiratnaṃ syamantakam /
dadau bhrātre narapatiḥ premṇā satrājiduttamam //
2.71.d:
स प्रसेनाय तद्दिव्यं मणिरत्नं स्यमन्तकम् ।
ददौ भ्रात्रे नरपतिः प्रेम्णा सत्राजिदुत्तमम् ॥
2.71.m: King Satrājit out of love gave that divine, best of jewel-gems, / the Syamantaka, to his brother Prasena.

2.71.s:
syamantako nāma maṇiryasminrāṣṭre sthito bhavet /
kāmavarṣī ca parjanyo na ca vyādhibhayaṃ tathā //
2.71.d:
स्यमन्तको नाम मणिर्यस्मिन्राष्ट्रे स्थितो भवेत् ।
कामवर्षी च पर्जन्यो न च व्याधिभयं तथा ॥
2.71.m: In whatever realm the gem named Syamantaka is kept, / Parjanya rains according to desire, and there is no fear of disease.

2.71.s:
lipsāṃ cakre prasenāttu maṇiratnaṃ syamantakam /
govindo na ca taṃ lebhe śakto 'pi na jahāra ca //
2.71.d:
लिप्सां चक्रे प्रसेनात्तु मणिरत्नं स्यमन्तकम् ।
गोविन्दो न च तं लेभे शक्तो ऽपि न जहार च ॥
2.71.m: Govinda desired to obtain that jewel-gem, the Syamantaka, from Prasena; / yet he did not get it, and though capable, he did not seize it.

2.71.s:
kadhācinmṛgayāṃ yātaḥ prasenastena bhūṣitaḥ /
syamantakakṛte siṃhādvadhaṃ prāpa sudāruṇam //
2.71.d:
कधाचिन्मृगयां यातः प्रसेनस्तेन भूषितः ।
स्यमन्तककृते सिंहाद्वधं प्राप सुदारुणम् ॥
2.71.m: Once Prasena, adorned with it, went on a hunt; / on account of the Syamantaka, he met a terrible death from a lion.

2.71.s:
jāṃbavānṛkṣarājastu taṃ siṃhaṃ nijaghāna vai /
ādāya ca maṇiṃ divyaṃ svabilaṃ praviveśa ha //
2.71.d:
जांबवानृक्षराजस्तु तं सिंहं निजघान वै ।
आदाय च मणिं दिव्यं स्वबिलं प्रविवेश ह ॥
2.71.m:
Then Jāmbavat, the king of the bears, struck down that lion,
and having taken the divine jewel, entered his own cave.

2.71.s:
tatkarma kṛṣṇasya tato vṛṣṇyandhakamahattarāḥ /
maṇiṃ gṛdhnostu manvānāstameva viśaśaṅkire //
2.71.d:
तत्कर्म कृष्णस्य ततो वृष्ण्यन्धकमहत्तराः ।
मणिं गृध्नोस्तु मन्वानास्तमेव विशशङ्किरे ॥
2.71.m:
